g-afc-m23.name: AFC/M23
g-afc-m23.role: Armed movement (Alliance Fleuve Congo / M23), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: Human Rights Watch reported that its research and the United Nations indicate that the M23's Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Masozera directed military training with support from other M23 officers, and that Rwandan military trainers operated in both Rumangabo and Tshanzu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that 'Colonel' Gafishi Semikobe Simon was officially appointed AFC/M23 'Officer for Mobilisation and Recruitment' on 11 February 2025 and also carried out responsibilities relating to the 'security files'.
The UN Group of Experts reported that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by "Lieutenant-Colonel" Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement, led by "Lieutenant -Colonel" Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August 2025; it described these as support to MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 confiscated identification documents, including voter cards and land titles of the refugees, and publicly burned them in the presence of AFC/M23 officials, including AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda, military spokesperson Willy Ngoma and Goma's military commander, 'Colonel' Nsanze Nzamuye Jimmy, and in the presence of local media.

The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9–11 June (2025), claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.
The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres.
The UN Group of Experts reported that the overall military command of AFC/M23 remained under 'General' Sultani Makenga, with political leadership held by Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa remained in frequent contact with Makenga, Bisimwa and 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze, and that the military and political leadership of AFC/M23 continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 maintained two principal intelligence entities: the Directorate of Security and Intelligence, headed by Basile Gasigwa (a.k.a. 'Gas'), and a military intelligence unit led by 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze.
The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 sources confirmed 'Colonel' Léon Kanyamibwa was in command of all training centres, with the support of AFC/M23 and Rwandan trainers.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, after AFC/M23 reinforcements led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, a second reinforcement led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Oscar Ndabagaza was blocked as it attempted to cross hostile areas before finally reaching Mikenge at the end of August.
Announced through its justice-revival commission the integration of 378 new magistrates into its judicial system
Reported by Kivu Morning Post to have taken control of Buhimba and Mahanga
UN Group of Experts estimated AFC/M23 combat strength at around 30,000 elements
UN Group of Experts reported AFC/M23-occupied territories divided into three defence zones
Accused the Congolese army and its allies in a communiqué of air strikes on Bidegu and surroundings
Alliance Fleuve Congo listed as an entity in the SECO consolidated annex

g-afc-m23.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-006"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that the overall military command of AFC/M23 remained under 'General' Sultani Makenga, with political leadership held by Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-011"></sup>

g-arc.name: ARC (Armée révolutionnaire congolaise)
g-arc.role: Military wing named as ARC, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 14 September AFC/M23 publicized the 'pass-out' of 7,437 'commandos' who had finished their training in Rumangabo; that the graduation ceremony was presided over by 'General' Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa, who said the cohort would form four brigades of 'commando' units; and that the Group could not independently confirm the number of 7,437 announced by AFC/M23.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the North Kivu governor under AFC/M23 administration, Bahati Musanga Erasto, began a tour of Bwito collectivity, Rutshuru territory, on 12 February 2026, visiting Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe) and Nyanzale, and that at the end of the tour more than twenty young people were recruited into the ARC.

Congovirtuel reported, citing Africa Intelligence, that Théo Binamungu, described as a close political adviser to Nangaa, was arrested at the end of August by loyalists of Makenga, interrogated by the military intelligence of the Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) and then by the Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), and transferred to Munzenze central prison on 8 September.

Kivu Morning Post reported that FARDC brigadier general François Kamanzi, commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central, had joined the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) led by Joseph Kabila; FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said he joined the ranks of the 'Lions de Sarambwe' within the Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC).

g-arc.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that sources reported on 16 September 2025 the deployment of at least 15 fully loaded trucks with AFC/M23 combatants coming from the AFC/M23-ARC training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga, in Lubero territory, two days after a pass-out ceremony. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-NKN-FRONT-011"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that on 14 September AFC/M23 publicized the 'pass-out' of 7,437 'commandos' who had finished their training in Rumangabo; that the graduation ceremony was presided over by 'General' Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa, who said the cohort would form four brigades of 'commando' units; and that the Group could not independently confirm the number of 7,437 announced by AFC/M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-018"></sup>

g-rdf.name: RDF
g-rdf.role: Rwandan armed forces (Rwanda Defence Force), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF had established a base on Idjwi island, often used for troop deployments and rotations via Lake Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that each M23 combat unit was supervised and supported by RDF, and that RDF personnel were integrated into mixed battalions alongside M23 elements, including commando units originating from Bigogwe, Rubavu and Cyangugu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain, and that the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition continued to contest AFC/M23 and RDF advances on multiple fronts.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in January and February 2025 a conservative estimate of 6,000 RDF troops, including RDF special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.
UN Group of Experts estimated at least 6,000 RDF troops active in North Kivu and northern South Kivu in January and February 2025
UN Group of Experts documented soldiers of RDF 107, 135 and 109 Brigades in North Kivu in February and March 2025
The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres.

The UN Group of Experts conservatively estimated that between 6,000 and 7,000 RDF personnel remained deployed across North and South Kivu at the time of drafting, comprising at least two brigades and two special forces battalions.

The Group of Experts reported that the offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu, and that AFC/M23 and RDF sources had signaled since early October the intent of taking Uvira, pointing at a carefully planned operation by AFC/M23 and Rwanda.

The UN Group of Experts reported that one RDF brigade operated within AFC/M23's 'first defence zone' (Goma, Nyiragongo, Binza, Bwito, Rutshuru, and Kanyabayonga, Kirumba and Kipese in Lubero), and another RDF brigade in the 'second defence zone' (Masisi, Walikale, Bibwe, Kalembe, and South Kivu areas including Walungu, Mwenga and Minembwe).
UN Group of Experts estimated RDF deployment at 8,000 to 10,000 in South Kivu and 6,000 to 8,000 in North Kivu

The UN Group of Experts reported that as of mid-February 2026 RDF deployments in South Kivu were approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain-Moyens Plateaux axis, 800 in the Hauts Plateaux, 1,800 along the Ngweshe-Mwenga axis, and an undetermined number elsewhere including in the direction of Fizi.

The UN Group of Experts reported that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux; the Group also noted that RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23.
The United States announced sanctions on the RDF and four senior officers, per SOS Médias Burundi

The UN Group of Experts reported that the individuals designated by OFAC were Vincent Nyakarundi, Chief of Staff of the RDF; Major-General Ruki Karusisi, commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander; General Mubarakh Muganga, Chief of Defence Staff; and Stanislas Gashugi, Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025.
DRC representative told the Security Council that a TB2 drone strike attributed to the Rwandan Defense Forces hit a Congolese position at Pinga

g-rdf.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF had established a base on Idjwi island, often used for troop deployments and rotations via Lake Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-028"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-RDF-002"></sup>

g-fardc.name: FARDC
g-fardc.role: Congolese national armed forces, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission)
latin: Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain, and that the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition continued to contest AFC/M23 and RDF advances on multiple fronts.

The UN Group of Experts assessed that control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens the influence of AFC/M23 over the northern 'gate' of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.

The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting.

The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.
The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF took Bukavu on 16 February, Government authorities, FDNB and FARDC withdrew towards Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura in Burundi.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, to restore security, the FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu governorate were relocated to Uvira in early March, and that in early April DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and former RAD national coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to appease the Wazalendo groups.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its report, relations between FARDC and Wazalendo had improved and some Wazalendo groups had left the centre of Uvira at the request of FARDC command.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its final report, the AFC/M23 controlled mining areas in Kalehe, Walungu and Mwenga territories as far as Kamanyola in the south, while the FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo kept control of the Ruzizi plain and held positions along the Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira road, blocking the AFC/M23 advance towards Uvira.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.

The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.

The UN Secretary-General reported that in South Kivu, Twirwaneho and M23 pushed back FARDC outside of the general Minembwe area and regained control of Point Zero on 4 July, effectively restoring the frontline to its late January 2026 configuration.

g-fardc.summary: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2025-012"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-017"></sup>

g-wazalendo.name: Wazalendo
g-wazalendo.role: Coalition of pro-government local armed groups, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)

timeline.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23.

Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said Rushaba had been with Nyamusaraba in the 'Task force' together with the Burundian forces before deserting it, starting clashes at Kashama and allying with the M23. The article describes the Task force as composed of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo, and quotes another source on site as saying there was a coalition of Banyamulenge based in Kahololo/Marungu, Rushaba wazalendo and M23 elements from Kaziba.
Human Rights Watch reported concern over the army lacking command and control over the Wazalendo
Actualite.cd reported that fighting resumed on the morning of Sunday 10 August 2025 between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo militiamen at Mulamba, Walungu territory, according to its sources.

A UN Peacebuilding Support Office briefing on the DRC (September 2025) stated that Uvira had been at the center of tensions, both in relation to a possible AFC/M23 advance and to growing strain between the FARDC and wazalendo factions.

In an analysis of the cohabitation of FARDC and Wazalendo at Uvira, RFI said that Wazalendo and FARDC do not always obey the same hierarchy and that the Wazalendo are groups organised in quasi-autonomous entities, each answering directly to its chief.

Amnesty International said that the FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition, and that the DRC's finance minister told the National Assembly's Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$4 million per month.
UN Group of Experts reported South Kivu Wazalendo divided into at least three coordinations

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that around 16:00 on Monday 6 April 2026 several places in the Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory (Kaziba, Katale, Kafufula, Katanga, Mpanama, Braza, Bushege and Lulamba) had already passed under AFC/M23 control after fighting with wazalendo.

Actualite.cd reported that Tushunguti (Kalehe) was again under FARDC control, supported by wazalendo fighters, after a brief AFC/M23 occupation that began on 7 April 2026; it said the counter-offensive was launched from the Biriko and Busurungi axes in Walikale.
Elements held a checkpoint where an MSF team was stopped between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the shooting at Kibati had stopped after a day of fighting reported on Thursday in the area, and that the FARDC and wazalendo maintained their presence in the centre of Kibati while the AFC/M23 rebels controlled the hills overlooking the town.

Actualite.cd reported on 18 September that the centre of Kibati, in Luberike groupement (Walikale), had returned under AFC/M23 control after the withdrawal of the FARDC and wazalendo, who had briefly occupied Kibati and advanced to Milonge, about five kilometres along the Kibati-Kashebere axis.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting resumed early on Friday 25 September between AFC/M23 and the FARDC supported by wazalendo at Remeka, Ufamandu 1er groupement (Masisi), about a week after the FARDC and wazalendo retook the centre of Remeka in a counter-offensive; AFC/M23 reportedly attacked with reinforcements from Ngungu.

Journal de Kinshasa reported that the attack on Pinga came only 24 hours after the FARDC, supported by wazalendo, retook several positions around Mindjendje, notably Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa and Luola.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting began on Saturday 24 October when the army and wazalendo attacked the positions of the FRN rebels on the Rushihe hill overlooking Katobo (Banamulindwa, Kisimba groupement, Walikale), and that the government coalition dislodged the rebels and took control of the position.

g-fdlr.name: FDLR
g-fdlr.role: Rwandan Hutu-led armed group (FDLR), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that key FDLR commanders and combatants were compelled to relocate to localities in Rutshuru, Masisi and Nyiragongo territories, and that FDLR military commander and sanctioned individual "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawunguka (alias Omega) and other key leaders, fearing RDF attacks, withdrew to the vicinity of the Nyiragongo volcano and inside Virunga National Park.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR combatants remained embedded within several VDP/Wazalendo groups, notably CMC/FDP, FDDP and APCLS, reinforcing their ranks while obscuring affiliation with FDLR.
UN Group of Experts reported the FDLR fragmented into three principal factions, with 3,500 to 4,500 combatants estimated

The UN Group of Experts reported that the FDLR-FOCA military commander was "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and its political leader "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro); that the overall FDLR-RUD leader was "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva (alias Faida/Fayida Hakimu); and that the FDLR-FPP leader was "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana (alias Dan Simplice).

The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing (its letter of 5 June 2026) the FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions, FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP), and that all three had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation.

The UN Group of Experts reported that "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader respectively; it named "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva as overall FDLR-RUD leader and "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana as FDLR-FPP leader.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the traditional FDLR-RUD area of operations was in the Bwisha and Bwito chefferies, Rutshuru territory, and that at the time of drafting FDLR-RUD units were particularly active in Jomba, Binza, Busanza and Bukoma, overlapping with the FDLR-FPP area in Rutshuru territory.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR sources claimed the group's overall strength exceeded 10,000 combatants, while United Nations and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.

The US State Department said on 2 June 2026 that it was designating John Imani Nzenze, chief of intelligence for the Rwanda-backed M23, 'an armed group that has committed killings, serious human rights abuses, and attacks on civilians in eastern DRC', and Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, saying the FDLR had 'committed sexual violence'.

The US State Department spokesperson said that the United States was designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, and said the FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence and launched cross-border attacks.
Its leader Sebastien Uwimbabazi listed in the SECO consolidated annex, address Rutshuru
DRC Government announced that a faction of FDLR elements had signed a protocol on disarmament, demobilization and cantonment; Rwanda rejected the plan

g-twirwaneho.name: Twirwaneho
g-twirwaneho.role: Armed group (Twirwaneho / MRDP-Twirwaneho), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Moïse Nyarugabo, a former Congolese senator and key member of Mr. Kabila's inner circle, rose to increasing prominence within the movement; the Group said, citing its earlier reports (S/2021/560 and S/2025/446), that he was a key figure in MRDP/Twirwaneho without holding a formal position, and that he represented MRDP/Twirwaneho interests in high-level meetings with Mr. Kabila and AFC/M23 leadership.

The Group of Experts reported that Charles Sematama assumed the military command of Twirwaneho and announced its alliance with AFC/M23 on 23 February 2025, and that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.

The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by "Lieutenant-Colonel" Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement, led by "Lieutenant -Colonel" Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August 2025; it described these as support to MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux.

The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's August 2025 note on Fizi territory listed local armed groups, including Twirwaneho, led by deserter colonel Charles Sematama after the death of Michel Rukundo alias Makanika and active in Balala Nord grouping.

The UN Group of Experts (final report S/2026/466, citing its earlier report S/2025/446, para. 176) reported that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.

The UN Group of Experts reported that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux; the Group also noted that RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23.

The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 elements consolidated around Banyamulenge population centres, including Minembwe, Mikenge and Muranvia, and that RDF presence in the Hauts Plateaux was limited to sporadic, platoon-sized specialized elements and air support.
The UN Group of Experts reported in its final report that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.

The UN Secretary-General reported that in South Kivu, Twirwaneho and M23 pushed back FARDC outside of the general Minembwe area and regained control of Point Zero on 4 July, effectively restoring the frontline to its late January 2026 configuration.

7sur7.cd reported that the UN sanctions listing included Colonel Charles Sematama, military chief of the Twirwaneho group, active in the Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu and accused of abuses against civilians.
Listed in the SECO consolidated annex, which states it has been involved in atrocities in the South-Kivu province
Radio Okapi reported that the two entities added to the UN sanctions list were the Alliance Fleuve Congo and the armed group Twirwaneho.

g-twirwaneho.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported in its final report that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-003"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux; the Group also noted that RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-015"></sup>

g-adf.name: ADF
g-adf.role: Armed group (Allied Democratic Forces), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The Sentry listed Meya Sebagala (Mzee Mayor) among key ADF leaders present along Baluku at Madina camp, citing its interviews with military intelligence, civil society representatives and local researchers in eastern DRC in January 2026.

The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.
Actualite.cd reported that since June 2024 Bapere (Lubero) has hosted two ADF groups, including the one led by Abwakasi, which it described as known for its harsh and deadly methods.
Attack in the Babila-Bakaiko farming zones attributed to ADF by Radio Okapi, at least 26 killed

The UN Group of Experts reported that two ADF units, led by "Mzee" Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province and by sanctioned commander Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, alias Abwakasi (CDi.040), in Lubero territory, were responsible for most ADF mass casualty attacks, and that supply rendezvous sites were overseen by senior ADF figures including Mzee Meya, Abwakasi and Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender.
Commander Muhammed Lumisa listed in the SECO consolidated annex

The Sentry reported that Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (also known as Abwakasi) leads operations along the Lubero-Bapere-Manguredjipa axis, with headquarters in Lohoa and positions across Batike, Baredje and Bapukara.

g-adf.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-009"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that two ADF units, led by "Mzee" Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province and by sanctioned commander Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, alias Abwakasi (CDi.040), in Lubero territory, were responsible for most ADF mass casualty attacks, and that supply rendezvous sites were overseen by senior ADF figures including Mzee Meya, Abwakasi and Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007"></sup>

g-fdnb.name: FDNB
g-fdnb.role: Burundian armed forces (FDNB), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
latin: Forces de défense nationales du Burundi (FDNB)
Force nationale de défense du Burundi (FNDB)
Force de défense nationale du Burundi

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain, and that the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition continued to contest AFC/M23 and RDF advances on multiple fronts.

The UN Group of Experts assessed that control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens the influence of AFC/M23 over the northern 'gate' of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.

The Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with the FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain: FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover, and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.

The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.
The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF took Bukavu on 16 February, Government authorities, FDNB and FARDC withdrew towards Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura in Burundi.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably in the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB (supported by FARDC and Wazalendo) and AFC/M23 (supported by RDF) resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 approximately 14 FDNB battalions under the 'Task Force Congo' (TAFOC) umbrella were still on DRC territory, of which 10 were reportedly in the Ruzizi Plain, two in and around Uvira and two in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its final report, the AFC/M23 controlled mining areas in Kalehe, Walungu and Mwenga territories as far as Kamanyola in the south, while the FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo kept control of the Ruzizi plain and held positions along the Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira road, blocking the AFC/M23 advance towards Uvira.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that during his visit to Uvira on a Monday (dateline 7 April 2025), Defence Minister Guy Kabombo, accompanied by Lieutenant General Padiri Bulenda (national coordinator of the Wazalendo) and a Burundian army delegation, praised the commitment of the Burundian army, the Burundian National Defence Force (FDNB); SOS Médias Burundi stated in its own narration that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10.000 soldiers in the DRC.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that on the Wednesday before its publication the FARDC chief of staff, Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe, and his Burundian counterpart, General Prime Niyongabo, head of the FDNB, crossed the border at Kavimvira escorted by a large Burundian military contingent and headed to the 'Sokola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu' operational sector, where they held a closed meeting; they left around 16:50 for Bujumbura without a statement to the press.
Criticised by Wazalendo militias for not conducting offensives against the M23 while present in Uvira, per SOS Médias Burundi

The UN Group of Experts reported that during more than a month of controlling Uvira, AFC/M23 forced the withdrawal of FDNB, captured large FARDC bases and dominated the entire Ruzizi plain along the Burundian border, and that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.
Bombardment of Ilundu/Basita village attributed to the FARDC and the FDNB by a local civilian-protection network

g-red-tabara.name: RED Tabara
g-red-tabara.role: Burundian armed group (RED Tabara), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux; the Group also noted that RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23.

The UN Group of Experts reported that RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory) and Kipupu (Mwenga territory), and that RED Tabara leadership had repeatedly denied links with AFC/M23 while its combatants took part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that the troop movements it described came a few days after the retaking of positions at Magunda and Malimba by Burundian soldiers, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen, positions it said had reportedly been occupied earlier by RED-Tabara fighters; it said these operations followed clashes reported in the Masango area that reportedly cost the lives of seven Burundian soldiers, according to the information reported.

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe.

g-fnl-zabampema.summary: Factuel.cd reported that on Thursday 6 November 2025 fighting continued for the third consecutive day in the Itombwe highlands (Mwenga territory), opposing Wazalendo of the Front de Défense du Congo (FDCC), led by General Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin, to a rebel coalition of AFC-M23, RDF, Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and FNL/Zabampema; per local sources the fighting was particularly violent around Tuwetuwe, where the coalition tried to take a FARDC-held position and FARDC supported by FDCC Wazalendo repelled the attack. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q4-012"></sup> Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-006"></sup>

latin: CMC (Collectif des mouvements pour le changement)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and his troops were based in Lukweti, Masisi territory, while CMC-FDP, led by Dominique Ndaruhutse, was in Virunga National Park fighting in areas including Katsiru, Rwindi, Bukombo, Bambo, Tongo and Kalengera in Rutshuru territory.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR combatants remained embedded within several VDP/Wazalendo groups, notably CMC/FDP, FDDP and APCLS, reinforcing their ranks while obscuring affiliation with FDLR.
Fighters reported by Radio Okapi to have ambushed an AFC-M23 patrol at Mashango village, Bwito

Amnesty International described Dominique 'Domi' Kamanzi Ndaruhutse as CMC-FDP's top commander and said he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and has, according to the UN Group of Experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru's Bwito area.

g-frn.name: FRN
g-frn.role: Political-military movement (Front pour la refondation de la nation), as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
latin: FRN (Front pour la Refondation de la Nation)
Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)

timeline.text: Radio Maendeleo reported on 20 October that after the Wazalendo offensive that led to their entry into Shanje, Lumbishi and Numbi between 5 and 6 October, a counter-offensive had allowed troops of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) to retake control of them.

BBC News Afrique reported that the creation of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), with Joseph Kabila as president, was announced by FRN adviser Claude Ibalanky at a joint press conference at the former president's residence in Goma, a city controlled by the M23; BBC described the FRN as replacing the AFC-M23, and reported that Kabila would have as deputies the rebel leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki and Sultani Makenga.

Actualite.cd reported that the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), led by Joseph Kabila, announced in a political declaration dated 12 October in Goma that it ended the existence of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, which it 'succeeds by right', and aims to fight Kinshasa 'by all means including force'.

BBC News reported that former president Joseph Kabila was named leader of a new rebel coalition, announced at a press conference at his residence in Goma by the coalition's adviser Claude Ibalanky, with M23 leader Sultani Makenga as one of Kabila's four deputies and the other three also from the AFC-M23 alliance; BBC said the Congolese government had not commented.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the Wazalendo launched the attack on a Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) position at Kiseguro on Tuesday morning and, after several hours of fighting, withdrew from the area, leaving the positions in the hands of the FRN rebels.
Spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said Kinshasa coalition forces were bombarding Rugezi, per Kivu Morning Post
Accused government forces of bombarding Rugezi on 17 to 18 October, per Kivu Morning Post
Actualite.cd reported that after the AFC/M23 withdrawal from Uvira city and the Ruzizi plain under US pressure in December 2025, the rebels had positioned themselves at Kamanyola.

Actualite.cd reported that other rebels had taken the direction of villages of the Itara-Luvungi groupement, notably Katogota, Bulinga and Kinyinya near Mugobe, and another part had settled in the Kigoma highlands (Kageregere and surroundings).

Kivu Morning Post reported that the vice-presidents of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), Corneille Nangaa and Bertrand Bisimwa, presented the FRN's organisation in Goma on Wednesday 21 October, and that Nangaa set out an institutional architecture of four organs including a Collège des fondateurs of 20 members and a Conseil de la révolution of five members.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting began on Saturday 24 October when the army and wazalendo attacked the positions of the FRN rebels on the Rushihe hill overlooking Katobo (Banamulindwa, Kisimba groupement, Walikale), and that the government coalition dislodged the rebels and took control of the position.

Radio Maendeleo reported that FRN troops were said to have concentrated their positions on Mitimbili hill, between the Muhumba and Kabembe groupements, while Wazalendo fighters were said to be positioned on the Nshoko hills in the Kahungwe groupement.
Taarifa Rwanda reported, citing frontline sources, that FRN fighters captured the Kahwizi (Kawizi) locality less than 10 kilometres from Uvira city.

The Rio Times reported that Taarifa wrote on 27 October that FRN fighters had captured the villages of Gitabo, Nyabigega and Mangwa, and had taken Kuwamabuye, Nyarurango and Rugomero, heading toward Runingu.
FRN spokesperson confirmed that a former FARDC operations commander had joined its military wing

g-frn.summary: Actualite.cd reported that thousands of families who fled clashes between the FRN and the FARDC supported by Wazalendo in the Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, were living in difficult conditions at Nyabibwe, lacking food, shelter and basic necessities, mostly women and children. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2026Q4-015"></sup> Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN vice-president Bertrand Bisimwa, in a speech at Bukavu on Thursday, defended continued teaching in FRN-held zones despite measures by the Congolese government, and that the FRN promised to support teachers whose pay had been suspended by Kinshasa. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2026Q4-018"></sup>

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR combatants remained embedded within several VDP/Wazalendo groups, notably CMC/FDP, FDDP and APCLS, reinforcing their ranks while obscuring affiliation with FDLR.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the "Synergie Masisi-Walikale", comprising 17 armed groups, was led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa (CDi.033), and that FDLR-FOCA combatants were integrated into the Masisi-Walikale and Petit Nord synergies.

g-ndc-r.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, that violent clashes on Sunday 31 May at Yaki, between Kashebere and Miba in Luberike groupement (Walikale), opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the NDC-Rénové group led by Guidon Shimiray. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H1-010"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that, with FARDC counter-offensive operations affected by troop shortages, FARDC relied increasingly on Wazalendo armed groups against ADF, including the UPLC led by "General" Germain Kambale Mayani, elements of the NDC-R of sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, and a local APCLS detachment led by "General" Fimbo. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-010"></sup>

g-cnpsc.role: Wazalendo armed group (CNPSC, associated with Yakutumba), as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that for more than a week fighting had opposed the Wazalendo of the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC) of William Amuri Yakutumba to certain elements of the Biloze Bishambuke self-defence forces of Kalembe Ngoma Nzito, and quoted an elected official from Uvira, president of the defence and security commission of the provincial assembly, as saying the clashes began on 25 October 2025 and caused loss of life.
The UN Group of Experts reported that in January 2026 CNPSC, through its "finance bureau", published a comprehensive list of taxes across multiple sectors.

The Group of Experts reported that the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC), led by Yakutumba, maintained a parallel administration in areas it controlled, particularly in Fizi territory, that in January 2026 its 'finance bureau' published a list of taxes across multiple sectors, and that since 2023 it had operated a parallel judicial system with detention facilities, former detainees reporting release conditioned on payment of fines of 2,000,000 to 5,000,000 Congolese francs.

g-landa-bango.summary: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January the Mai-Mai Kuruninga killed a boy in Kalundu quarter and a man in Kabindula quarter, and the Mai-Mai Landa Bango killed a woman in Sondo quarter, in Uvira city. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-026"></sup>

g-fpp-ap.name: FPP/AP
g-fpp-ap.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
latin: FPP/AP (Force des patriotes pour la paix / Armée du peuple)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a public declaration from Mbwavinywa, three armed groups announced their break with Kinshasa to join the M23/AFC: the FPP/AP of the self-proclaimed general Kabido, the NDC-R/M and Maï-Maï Kifuafua.

Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented in Beni two VDP (Wazalendo) of the Maï-Maï group Force des patriotes pour la paix/Armée du peuple (FPP/AP), led by the self-proclaimed general Kabido, who surrendered to the FARDC following their leader's rallying to the M23.

Mediacongo reported that the self-proclaimed general Kabido and his armed group FPP/AP had officially joined the AFC-M23, which it described as a politico-military movement backed by Rwanda according to several national and international reports, and that the self-proclaimed general Shimiray Guidon, described as the commander of the Wazalendo across North Kivu, condemned this act of treason in a communiqué.

The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies.

g-fpp-ap.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented in Beni two VDP (Wazalendo) of the Maï-Maï group Force des patriotes pour la paix/Armée du peuple (FPP/AP), led by the self-proclaimed general Kabido, who surrendered to the FARDC following their leader's rallying to the M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2025H1-008"></sup> The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-CMD-001"></sup>

g-copaco.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 9 April Wazalendo of COPACO and MCDPN, commanded by self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho, Maike and Bahige, recovered Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 and Nyawaronga on the Kalehe highlands after fighting with M23 backed by Rwanda.

Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye.

g-copaco.summary: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2026Q2-002"></sup> Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 9 April Wazalendo of COPACO and MCDPN, commanded by self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho, Maike and Bahige, recovered Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 and Nyawaronga on the Kalehe highlands after fighting with M23 backed by Rwanda. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2025Q2-001"></sup>

g-updf.name: UPDF
g-updf.role: Ugandan armed forces (UPDF), as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that in Beni and Butembo social groups rose up to protest the withdrawal from Lubero of the Ugandan soldiers deployed in the DRC under the joint FARDC-UPDF operations.

BETO reported that M23 elements withdrew from Friday 7 March from three villages of Lubero territory, Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, about 45 km west of Lubero centre, after intense clashes between the FARDC supported by VDP and the M23; it also said the Ugandan army (UPDF) had for some weeks occupied the neighbouring village since the M23 threatened Lubero-centre.

Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC and the Ugandan army (UPDF) retook control of Muhola hill in Baswagha chiefdom on Friday 4 July, described as a stronghold of a Maï-Maï group led by a commander nicknamed « Le Blanc », a week after intense fighting.

Radio Okapi reported that, a week after the launch of the joint offensive, regular forces retook control of several localities south of Lubero, including Mabambi, Kalundu, Kivugha and Maboya, that the fighting caused major displacement of local populations, and that the targeted Maï-Maï group is accused by local authorities of multiple abuses against civilians.
Radio Okapi reported that the Kalangira clashes took place near the buffer zone controlled by the Ugandan army, deployed for eight months to contain the rebels' advance towards Lubero-Centre.

The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.

g-updf.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-009"></sup> The Group of Experts reported, for the 2025 cases verified by the UN, that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of victims (M23 ranked first, followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions) and State agents for 19 per cent (FARDC soldiers first, followed by the PNC), and that the UPDF, the FNDB and RED-Tabara were also responsible for CRSV cases. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-037"></sup>

g-raia-mutomboki.name: Raia Mutomboki
g-raia-mutomboki.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)
g-raia-mutomboki.summary: The Group of Experts reported, citing a UN source, that for the January 2026 verified cases armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims (M23 most, with 21 victims, then Nyatura four, Raïa Mutomboki three and ADF two), while State agents were responsible for 46 per cent of the cases, with FARDC soldiers ranking first, followed by the PNC and one official from the Ministry of Mines and Energy. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-030"></sup> BCNUDH reported that in January 2026 it documented at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims (39 women, 21 girls and one man), 59 per cent fewer than the 147 victims documented in December 2025, which it explained mainly by intensified fighting and insecurity that limited humanitarian access to victims and led to under-documentation. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2026-021"></sup>

g-fdlr-foca.name: FDLR-FOCA
g-fdlr-foca.role: Faction of the FDLR, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The Group of Experts reported that in late March 2026 a FARDC helicopter landed in Pinga to deliver weapons to FDLR-FOCA units led by 'Major-General' Uzabakiriho Cyprien that had been fighting AFC/M23 and RDF in Masisi territory, and that on 7 April a confidential encounter between a Kinshasa delegation including FARDC generals and the FDLR-FOCA high command in Pinga decided that FDLR-FARDC cooperation would continue.

The UN Group of Experts reported that the FDLR-FOCA military commander was "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and its political leader "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro); that the overall FDLR-RUD leader was "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva (alias Faida/Fayida Hakimu); and that the FDLR-FPP leader was "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana (alias Dan Simplice).

The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing (its letter of 5 June 2026) the FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions, FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP), and that all three had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation.

The UN Group of Experts reported that "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader respectively; it named "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva as overall FDLR-RUD leader and "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana as FDLR-FPP leader.

The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR-FOCA, the largest FDLR faction, remained active on several major front lines in North Kivu, notably in Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories, and that its special unit, the Commando de recherche et d'action en profondeur (CRAP), was reported to have active units on the outskirts of Goma and infiltrated in Goma town.

g-fdlr-foca.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader respectively; it named "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva as overall FDLR-RUD leader and "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana as FDLR-FPP leader. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-BI-FDLR-002"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing (its letter of 5 June 2026) the FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions, FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP), and that all three had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-BI-FDLR-001"></sup>

g-vdp.name: VDP
g-vdp.role: Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Human Rights Watch)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that FARDC Colonel Sekololo, based in Walikale, still acted as the liaison between FARDC and VDP, and that regular FARDC helicopter rotations to VDP/Wazalendo-held front lines in Walikale delivered uniforms, weapons, ammunition and food supplies.

BETO reported that M23 elements withdrew from Friday 7 March from three villages of Lubero territory, Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, about 45 km west of Lubero centre, after intense clashes between the FARDC supported by VDP and the M23; it also said the Ugandan army (UPDF) had for some weeks occupied the neighbouring village since the M23 threatened Lubero-centre.

Human Rights Watch reported that military and other sources estimate about 20,000 Wazalendo fighters, although the exact figure is unknown, and that in September 2023 some members of the coalition formed the Patriotic Defense Volunteers (VDP), an 'official' auxiliary force.
A VDP fighter prosecuted for rape received 20 years of servitude pénale principale from the Goma garrison military tribunal

g-sukola-2.name: Sokola 2
g-sukola-2.role: FARDC operation / sector (Sokola 2), as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that the appointments of brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba and Amuli Civiri as commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector followed the death in August of brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, former commander of the 33rd military region, and the replacement of general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste as commander of the operational sector.

Radio Okapi reported that brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques and Amuli Civiri, named respectively commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, arrived in Uvira on Wednesday 22 October 2025 via the Kavimvira border post with Burundi.
Sukola 2 Nord Sud-Kivu sector command reported at least three civilians killed and 18 wounded in bombardments in Buhavu, per ReelActu

g-sukola-2.summary: Radio Okapi reported that brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques and Amuli Civiri, named respectively commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, arrived in Uvira on Wednesday 22 October 2025 via the Kavimvira border post with Burundi. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-018"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that the appointments of brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba and Amuli Civiri as commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector followed the death in August of brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, former commander of the 33rd military region, and the replacement of general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste as commander of the operational sector. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-019"></sup>

u-sukola-2-sud.name: Sokola 2 Sud
u-sukola-2-sud.role: FARDC sector (Sokola 2 Sud, South Kivu), as named in the cited reports (first cited: 7sur7.cd)

timeline.text: 7sur7.cd reported on 22 October 2025 that newly appointed FARDC commanders had arrived in Uvira, among them brigade general Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques as new commander of the 33rd military region and general AMULI CIVIRI as commander of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.
Operation spokesperson said the FARDC retook Kashamata, Wihene and Kimete near Minembwe, per Radio Okapi
Its commander, Colonel Michel Apoko Bangala, reported two seriously wounded after bombs fell on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi-Centre
Operation spokesperson said the FARDC found a mass grave at Masango, per MediaCongo

u-sukola-2-sud.summary: 7sur7.cd reported on 22 October 2025 that newly appointed FARDC commanders had arrived in Uvira, among them brigade general Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques as new commander of the 33rd military region and general AMULI CIVIRI as commander of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-FARDC-005"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud-Sud operations confirmed that the points of divergence had been smoothed out and that the FARDC were securing the city, upstream and downstream, describing a misunderstanding maintained by a small group of Wazalendo. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q2-016"></sup>

u-fardc-33rd-military-region.name: FARDC 33rd military region
u-fardc-33rd-military-region.role: FARDC military region, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that the new commander of the 33rd military region, General Dunia, began on Tuesday 8 April the identification of Wazalendo fighters in Uvira, to distinguish genuine from false Wazalendo and give the government a list of those deserving benefits.

Radio Okapi reported that the appointments of brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba and Amuli Civiri as commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector followed the death in August of brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, former commander of the 33rd military region, and the replacement of general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste as commander of the operational sector.

Afrikarabia reported that President Félix Tshisekedi's appointment of General Olivier Gasita as deputy commander of the 33rd military region, and his taking up duty in Uvira on 1 September, were at the heart of the unrest, with civil society organisations and above all the Wazalendo militias leading the protest; SOS Médias Burundi reported that General Gasita was entrenched in an Uvira hotel under the joint protection of the FARDC and of 'militaires burundais'.

Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC supported brigadier general Olivier Gasita, contested by the Wazalendo and struggling to take up his functions as deputy commander of the 33rd military region in charge of military operations and intelligence at Uvira, South Kivu.

7sur7.cd reported on 22 October 2025 that newly appointed FARDC commanders had arrived in Uvira, among them brigade general Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques as new commander of the 33rd military region and general AMULI CIVIRI as commander of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.

7sur7.cd reported that the army spokesperson of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, sub-lieutenant Mbuyi Kalonji Reagan, said the new 33rd military region commander replaces the late brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, who died after feeling unwell while on duty, and that general Civiri replaces general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste.

Radio Okapi reported that brigadier generals Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques and Amuli Civiri, named respectively commander of the 33rd military region and commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, arrived in Uvira on Wednesday 22 October 2025 via the Kavimvira border post with Burundi.

SOS Médias Burundi reported that general Olivier Gasita, in charge of intelligence and operations in the 33rd military region, was not affected by the October 2025 reshuffle and remained in post despite demonstrations in Uvira in September; the same report said that, according to several local sources, he had left Uvira on 8 October 2025 and was staying in Kinshasa.

Congorassure.cd reported on 26 January 2026 that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien had been designated provisional commander of the 33rd military region, covering South Kivu and Maniema, according to an official note from the FARDC chief of general staff that the outlet said it had seen.

La Prunelle RDC reported that a voice message attributed to James « Fyeka Adui » was circulated on social networks, in which the author accused the commander of the 33rd military region of withholding funds meant for local Wazalendo armed groups; that he was summoned by the military intelligence services of the 33rd military region a few days after the message circulated; and that the Unité spéciale des Wazalendo pour les opérations au Sud-Kivu later announced his suspension as spokesperson.

u-fardc-33rd-military-region.summary: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC supported brigadier general Olivier Gasita, contested by the Wazalendo and struggling to take up his functions as deputy commander of the 33rd military region in charge of military operations and intelligence at Uvira, South Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-014"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that the new commander of the 33rd military region, General Dunia, began on Tuesday 8 April the identification of Wazalendo fighters in Uvira, to distinguish genuine from false Wazalendo and give the government a list of those deserving benefits. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q2-010"></sup>

u-fardc-34th-military-region.name: FARDC 34th military region
u-fardc-34th-military-region.role: FARDC military region, as named in the cited reports (first cited: the cited report)

timeline.text: Brigadier general Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin, commander of the 34th military region, reiterated his appeal for the surrender of the M23 members still active, the outlet reported.
Communication officer said the army foiled attacks attributed to the M23 at Katale, Mpanama and Kabulungu, per Ouragan.cd

u-fardc-34th-military-region.summary: Brigadier general Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin, commander of the 34th military region, reiterated his appeal for the surrender of the M23 members still active, the outlet reported. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-022"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that the staff of the 34th military region announced it had detained at Walikale two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and of violence that seriously affected civilians: self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COPACO movement (Coalition des Patriotes au Congo), and Musubao Kalimba, alias Kasilasi. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-001"></sup>

u-fardc-3rd-defence-zone.name: FARDC 3rd defence zone
u-fardc-3rd-defence-zone.role: FARDC defence zone, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: Published a communiqué condemning killings of civilians attributed to the RDF/M23/AFC coalition in South Kivu

u-fardc-3rd-defence-zone.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 September FARDC's 3rd Defense Zone command reported that it received 30 alleged AFC/M23-ARC combatants, including two minors, who surrendered voluntarily to the FARDC, while 15 others were captured during clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-048"></sup> Kivu Morning Post reported that a communiqué of the FARDC Third Defence Zone, signed by Major Nestor Mavudisa Kamba Mayoyo, spokesperson of 'cette zone militaire', said that 'ces ennemis de la paix' attacked FARDC positions at Kamatembe and Kalao (Mubuku groupement, Kalehe territory) on the morning of 12 July 2025, and that, according to the FARDC, another position was attacked at Batanga, Irambi Katana groupement, Kabare territory. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2025Q3-009"></sup>

u-guepard.name: Guépard
u-guepard.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission)

timeline.text: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting.

Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units.

u-guepard.summary: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2025-012"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q4-038"></sup>

u-hiboux.name: Hiboux
u-hiboux.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)

timeline.text: Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units.

u-hiboux.summary: Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q4-038"></sup> The Group of Experts reported that private military contractors accompanied FARDC when they entered Uvira in January 2026, that multiple drone strikes conducted with their support targeted AFC/M23 positions around Minembwe on 1 February 2026, and that between 2 and 8 February 2026 they airdropped FARDC 'Hiboux' special forces units at Point Zero. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-051"></sup>

u-simba-battalion.name: Simba battalion
u-simba-battalion.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: SOS Médias Burundi)

identifiers.value: 18 soldiers sentenced to death by the Uvira garrison military tribunal for cowardice at the front

timeline.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the 112 soldiers of the 21st battalion 'Simba' were prosecuted notably for abandoning, on the night of 23 August, strategic positions in the mountainous zones of Malimba and Masango in the Bijombo groupement while engaged in the defence of Uvira.

u-simba-battalion.summary: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the 112 soldiers of the 21st battalion 'Simba' were prosecuted notably for abandoning, on the night of 23 August, strategic positions in the mountainous zones of Malimba and Masango in the Bijombo groupement while engaged in the defence of Uvira. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q4-007"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced 18 soldiers of the Simba battalion to death for cowardice at the front in a verdict delivered on 4 September, without extenuating circumstances; the trial had opened on 23 August. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q3-021"></sup>

o-msf.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)
o-msf.role: Medical humanitarian organisation (MSF), as named in the cited reports (first cited: MSF)

timeline.text: MSF reported that the current frontline at Katogota in South Kivu bisects the road connecting Bukavu and Uvira, and that M23/AFC's position on Katogota was putting pressure on Uvira, which was under government control.

MSF said that Kamanyola, close to Katogota, was under M23/AFC control and had also seen its health system weakened by violence, and that while some stability had been restored in the town, most fighting continued in the surrounding hills, making access to fields impossible.
Said its team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu was stopped at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements

o-msf.summary: MSF said that the Hôpital Général de Référence in Uvira had repeatedly been caught in crossfire, endangering patients and staff, that medical activities had to be interrupted again the previous week with patients sheltering, and that armed men entered the hospital premises, moving and firing inside. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q1-011"></sup> MSF said that since January about fifteen incidents had directly affected teams, ambulances, offices and structures run or supported by MSF. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-NK-2025-005"></sup>

o-bcnudh.name: BCNUDH
o-bcnudh.role: UN Joint Human Rights Office, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its analysis for November 2025, stated that the Wazalendo also committed abuses in the context of internal clashes and interference in the administration of justice, notably in the city of Uvira.

o-bcnudh.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on the first half of 2025 accuses State agents of responsibility for sexual violence against 70 victims, including the FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UNHR-012"></sup> The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its analysis for November 2025, stated that the Wazalendo also committed abuses in the context of internal clashes and interference in the administration of justice, notably in the city of Uvira. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UV-SVHC-014"></sup>

o-pui.name: Première Urgence Internationale (PUI)
o-pui.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-pui.summary: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières was transferring its medical activities at Sake, Masisi territory, to Première Urgence Internationale after 13 months; in that period MSF teams treated more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence, and MSF said it was redirecting resources to other areas including Katoyi in Masisi. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-017"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) provided care to more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence at Sake, Masisi territory, over 13 months of intervention, and announced the transfer of its medical activities at Sake to Première Urgence Internationale (PUI). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2026Q4-006"></sup>

o-icrc.name: ICRC
o-icrc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Secretary-General)
latin: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
o-icrc.summary: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 7 August the DRC Government facilitated, through the International Committee of the Red Cross, the release and transfer to AFC/M23 of 15 detainees under the prisoner exchange protocol of the Doha Framework, and that AFC/M23 subsequently claimed that only 9 of the 15 individuals appeared on the list of 768 prisoners it had submitted. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-007"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that the transfer of fifteen detainees took place on 6 and 7 August, facilitated by the ICRC; the detainees left Beni, transited through Uganda and were handed to AFC/M23 in Rutshuru territory. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-DRC-2026-006"></sup>

o-gape.name: GAPE
o-gape.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
latin: Groupe d'action pour la protection de l'enfance
o-gape.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO Groupe d'action pour la protection de l'enfance (GAPE) said, in an interview on Wednesday 15 July 2026, that at least fifty-six children had been recruited by local armed militias, notably Wazalendo factions, in Walikale territory during the first two weeks of the school holidays; according to testimonies cited by GAPE's coordinator, the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily to join the groups. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-002"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-003"></sup>

o-pnc.name: Police nationale congolaise (PNC)
o-pnc.role: Congolese national police, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that the chef-lieu of Walungu territory was encircled, with the Wazalendo on one side and the M23 on the other, that the local administration was paralysed with its officials forced to live in hiding, and that the police and intelligence services were absent.

o-pnc.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on the first half of 2025 accuses State agents of responsibility for sexual violence against 70 victims, including the FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UNHR-012"></sup> BCNUDH reported that in the first half of 2026 armed groups were attributed 148 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 259 victims (M23 133 victims, Wazalendo 66, ADF 15, APCLS 11) and state agents 116 cases affecting 130 victims (FARDC 130 victims, PNC 6; as printed, the FARDC and PNC figures together exceed the State-agent total). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2026-011"></sup>

o-nouvelle-societe-civile.name: Nouvelle société civile congolaise
o-nouvelle-societe-civile.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that the Nouvelle société civile congolaise announced a partial suspension of the strike from Friday 5 September, after three days of a movement launched by Wazalendo combatants and citizen movements against the appointment of General Olivier Gasita as commander of operations and intelligence.

o-nouvelle-societe-civile.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the Nouvelle société civile congolaise announced a partial suspension of the strike from Friday 5 September, after three days of a movement launched by Wazalendo combatants and citizen movements against the appointment of General Olivier Gasita as commander of operations and intelligence. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q3-012"></sup> Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo have recovered Mikenge since Sunday 1 March, according to Pacifique Kararuka, president of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise at Kipupu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q1-012"></sup>

o-monusco.name: MONUSCO
o-monusco.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Secretary-General)

timeline.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that, with MONUSCO support, the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus conducted its first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August 2026 and a second mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September.
Transported 16 civilians by helicopter from Goma to Beni

o-monusco.summary: The UN Secretary-General reported that, with MONUSCO support, the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus conducted its first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August 2026 and a second mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-008"></sup> MONUSCO said that on 13 and 14 August, during incidents in Mayi-Moya (North Kivu), it provided physical protection to 206 civilians, including 70 women and 93 children, who sought refuge at its military base. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2025H2-008"></sup>

o-government-of-the-drc.name: Government of the DRC
o-government-of-the-drc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that President Félix Tshisekedi appointed commissioner Louis Segond Karawa vice-governor of North Kivu on Friday 7 March 2025, in the context of the occupation of Goma by the M23, and that he had been South Kivu provincial police commissioner from 2015.
Announced that a faction of FDLR elements had signed a protocol on disarmament, demobilization and cantonment
