o-government-of-the-drc.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published by its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-023"></sup> Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said on Monday in a statement posted on X that the government continued to work to avoid carnage and loss of life, as reported by AFP. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q1-002"></sup>

o-government-of-rwanda.name: Government of Rwanda
o-government-of-rwanda.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The Group of Experts reported that overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with 'General' Makenga, although his position was increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda, and that Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa remained the political leaders, all receiving instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.
Rejected the DRC plan on FDLR, arguing that the Washington Accords require verifiable neutralization of the FDLR

o-government-of-rwanda.summary: The Group of Experts reported that overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with 'General' Makenga, although his position was increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda, and that Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa remained the political leaders, all receiving instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-012"></sup> The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that, as a result of the past week's bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens had fled across the border to Bugarama in western Rwanda, where they were accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-RW-006"></sup>

g-nyatura.name: Nyatura
g-nyatura.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)
g-nyatura.summary: The Group of Experts reported, citing a UN source, that for the January 2026 verified cases armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims (M23 most, with 21 victims, then Nyatura four, Raïa Mutomboki three and ADF two), while State agents were responsible for 46 per cent of the cases, with FARDC soldiers ranking first, followed by the PNC and one official from the Ministry of Mines and Energy. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-030"></sup> The UN Secretary-General reported that on 17 June, in Masisi territory, at least 60 bodies were reportedly discovered following AFC/M23 operations against FDLR and Nyatura elements, as counter-FDLR operations continued to systematically target civilians, resulting in deaths and displacement. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-003"></sup>

o-human-rights-watch.name: Human Rights Watch
o-human-rights-watch.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Human Rights Watch)
o-human-rights-watch.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that the M23 abducted civilians into their forces during the Uvira occupation and that, in at least 12 documented cases, their whereabouts remain unknown. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2026-004"></sup> Human Rights Watch reported that it documented eight cases of rape by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira during the occupation that began in December 2025. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2026-001"></sup>

g-biloze-bishambuke.name: Biloze Bishambuke (FABB)
g-biloze-bishambuke.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's note)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that Wazalendo fighters allied to the Congolese army claimed to have taken control of Rugezi, Basimukuma grouping, Fizi, on Tuesday 20 May 2025 after night fighting with Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23; the claim came from Wazalendo spokesperson Aimable Nabulizi, who said the enemy had been dispersed.

The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's note said that the most important Maï-Maï factions in Fizi territory were those of Yakutumba, Ebuela (also known as Kibukila) and Biloze Bishambuke, which now collaborate with the FARDC under the name Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 and its allies, and that a coordination of Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 in Fizi territory was set up under the direction of Willam Yakutumba.

Kivu Morning Post reported that for more than a week fighting had opposed the Wazalendo of the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC) of William Amuri Yakutumba to certain elements of the Biloze Bishambuke self-defence forces of Kalembe Ngoma Nzito, and quoted an elected official from Uvira, president of the defence and security commission of the provincial assembly, as saying the clashes began on 25 October 2025 and caused loss of life.

g-biloze-bishambuke.summary: The Conflict Sensitivity Hub's note said that the most important Maï-Maï factions in Fizi territory were those of Yakutumba, Ebuela (also known as Kibukila) and Biloze Bishambuke, which now collaborate with the FARDC under the name Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 and its allies, and that a coordination of Wazalendo against the AFC/M23 in Fizi territory was set up under the direction of Willam Yakutumba. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-SKS-FIZI-023"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that at least four people were killed and valuables destroyed in clashes at Misisi and Lulimba, Fizi territory, between two Wazalendo factions: the CNCCP of commander Yakutumba and the FABB of Ngoma Nzito. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-004"></sup>

g-ancdh.name: ANCDH
g-ancdh.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-ancdh.summary: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 23-24-25 February 2025 the FARDC, with ANCDH and APCLS combatants, clashed in Kalembe, at the border between Masisi and Lubero territories. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-043"></sup> Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that men of Corneille Nangaa and Sultani Makenga (AFC/M23) attacked from the morning the positions of the Wazalendo of the ANCDH at Kalungu, after reinforcing their troops in men and equipment during the past week; the article places the fighting on the Tuesday and is dated Wednesday 9 July. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-NKW-MASISI-015"></sup>

g-pareco-ff.name: PARECO-FF
g-pareco-ff.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-pareco-ff.summary: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the same anonymous local human rights organisation and administrative sources, the Katoyi sector office was reportedly vandalised and looted at the beginning of April by Kigingi's militiamen. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-NKW-MASISI-013"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that, according to concordant sources, AFC-M23 rebels, described as supported by Rwanda, were fighting the VDP/Wazalendo of the group PARECO/FF in Ufamandu 2 (Katoyi sector, Masisi) on Saturday; the fighting began around 07 hours local time when M23 rebels attacked Wazalendo positions at Kahunda and Mitimingi, and residents fled towards Walikale territory or into the forest. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2025H2-007"></sup>

o-amnesty-international.name: Amnesty International
o-amnesty-international.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Amnesty International)

timeline.text: Said M23 fighters backed by Rwanda and Wazalendo groups committed atrocities including gang rapes, per Deutsche Welle Swahili
Published a report denouncing abuses by ADF rebels against civilians in North Kivu and Ituri

o-amnesty-international.summary: Amnesty International reported that more than 20 miners from Rubaya were kept in a pit and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-020"></sup> Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that, since taking Goma in January, the Rwanda-backed M23 had raided hospitals, abducted patients from their beds (civilians and hospitalised Congolese soldiers) and subjected them to torture. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2025-004"></sup>

o-butembo-lubero-garrison-military-tribu.name: Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal
o-butembo-lubero-garrison-military-tribu.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-butembo-lubero-garrison-military-tribu.summary: Actualite.cd reported that the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal convicted 25 people, 24 soldiers and one civilian, to 5 to 20 years in prison after mobile hearings held from 26 June to 8 July 2025 in Lubero-centre, that two soldiers were sentenced to death, and that the defendants were prosecuted for serious human rights violations including sexual violence, notably 14 cases of rape of minors, and murders of civilians. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2025H2-001"></sup> Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that the Butembo garrison military tribunal sentenced to death on Thursday 25 June 2026 four defendants (named in the source and listed in entities_named), whom the prosecution had pursued, two of them as Wazalendo, for criminal association, abductions followed by torture, and extortion, in the case of the abduction of 3 Egyptians and 9 Congolese; the defence said it would appeal. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2026H1-013"></sup>

o-cndh-rdc.name: CNDH-RDC
o-cndh-rdc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The CNDH-RDC)

timeline.text: Reported that M23 soldiers entered Muku and killed 6 civilians in reprisal for the alleged presence of Wazalendo

o-cndh-rdc.summary: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Sunday 29 June 2025 M23 soldiers killed 4 civilians in the locality of Kaniola (Walungu territory) and set fire to several civilians' houses. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-SK-2025-017"></sup> The Congolese National Human Rights Commission (CNDH-RDC) reported that on 19 April 2025 Pascaline NGWASI, coordinator of the Association des Mères Célibataires pour le Bien-être des Enfants Abandonnés, was arrested, beaten and raped by M23/AFC members in the Mabenga neighbourhood of Bukavu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-SK-2025-013"></sup>

g-synergie-wazalendo-front-grand-nord.name: Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord
g-synergie-wazalendo-front-grand-nord.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Grands Lacs News)
g-synergie-wazalendo-front-grand-nord.summary: Grands Lacs News reported that the Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord claimed the January 2026 operations against Tango Fort, saying it wanted to neutralise him and his supporters, accused of illegal detentions, torture, killings and arbitrary taxation, and that it welcomed the release of at least 11 illegally detained people, including minors, during the attack on the Lwamiso camp. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2026H1-016"></sup> Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the five presumed M23 fighters who surrendered in Lubero territory said, in their testimony, that they were former soldiers captured and forcibly enrolled during the fall of Goma to the M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2026H2-009"></sup>

u-m23-prc.name: M23/PRC (Police révolutionnaire congolaise)
u-m23-prc.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.

u-m23-prc.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-017"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that the newly established M23/PRC continued to conduct large-scale operations in Goma and Bukavu, resulting in arbitrary detentions and the forcible conscription of boys and men. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-044"></sup>

g-samidrc.name: SAMIDRC
g-samidrc.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-samidrc.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that the SADC stated in an official communiqué that 'SAMIDRC has not participated in any joint operations' and refuted AFC/M23's allegations, which it qualified as 'inaccurate and misleading'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-039"></sup> The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 23 January M23 and RDF launched a coordinated offensive on Sake, 25 km west of Goma, eventually overwhelming FARDC troops supported by MONUSCO and SAMIDRC as well as private military companies contracted by the Congolese Government. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-HRC-045"></sup>

o-cbca-ndosho-hospital.name: CBCA Ndosho hospital
o-cbca-ndosho-hospital.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Dr Sidibe Abdurahman, emergency physician at CBCA Ndosho hospital,)
o-cbca-ndosho-hospital.summary: Dr Sidibe Abdurahman, emergency physician at CBCA Ndosho hospital, said, as quoted by DW, that since January the hospital had received more than 1,000 patients against a capacity of 146 beds and was totally overwhelmed. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2025-006"></sup> The Group of Experts reported in an annex that on 3 March 2025 Fikiri Mwishuko, the Chef de groupement of Shanga, was abducted by AFC/M23 from the CBCA Ndosho hospital amongst other sick and wounded patients, and that he subsequently died, reportedly after having been tortured by AFC/M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-056"></sup>

o-ocha.name: OCHA
o-ocha.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: OCHA)
o-ocha.summary: OCHA reported that between 1 and 14 March 2025 clashes between the FARDC and the M23 continued in the Uvira Hauts Plateaux, affecting the localities of Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda and Muranvya. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q1-010"></sup> Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA monthly report, reported that on 18 July suspected ADF abducted 14 people in the locality of Bandulu, of whom seven hostages have since escaped, and that three days earlier 15 people had been abducted in the Bapere sector. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2025H2-004"></sup>

o-un-group-of-experts.name: UN Group of Experts
o-un-group-of-experts.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC)
o-un-group-of-experts.summary: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in such cases since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2026-023"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF had established a base on Idjwi island, often used for troop deployments and rotations via Lake Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-028"></sup>

o-haute-cour-militaire.name: Haute Cour militaire
o-haute-cour-militaire.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: BBC News Afrique)

timeline.text: BBC News Afrique reported that the verdict of the Haute Cour militaire in the trial of Joseph Kabila was delivered on a Tuesday after several postponements: the former Congolese president was sentenced to death by the court, which also ordered his immediate arrest.

Radio Okapi, citing ACP, reported that the High Military Court handed prison sentences of under five years to four general officers of the army and police accused of fleeing before the enemy in the east, and that its first president, lieutenant general magistrate Joseph Mutombo, announced that divisional commissioner Jean Romuald Ekuka, former vice-governor of North Kivu, was sentenced to 36 months in prison (the page prints the offence as 'libertété').

o-haute-cour-militaire.summary: BBC News Afrique reported that the verdict of the Haute Cour militaire in the trial of Joseph Kabila was delivered on a Tuesday after several postponements: the former Congolese president was sentenced to death by the court, which also ordered his immediate arrest. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-POL-2025-011"></sup> Radio Okapi, citing ACP, reported that the High Military Court president said deputy divisional commissioner Eddy Léonard Mukuna was sentenced to 24 months for cowardice, brigade general Papy Lupembe to 12 months for cowardice before the enemy, and Danny Yangba Tene to 12 months in prison for the same charge. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-FARDC-018"></sup>

g-android.name: Android
g-android.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
g-android.summary: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several local sources, fighting resumed early on 1 March 2025 in Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, where the Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Android elements allied to the M23 attacked Wazalendo positions. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKC-2025H1-002"></sup> Radio Okapi reported on 29 April 2025, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 rebels who had come from Nyangezi via Mushenyi were attacking FARDC and Wazalendo positions in the Kaziba chefferie (Walungu), and that from Kaziba the rebels were progressing toward Minembwe in the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi while another group advanced toward Luhwinja. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q2-015"></sup>

g-gumino.name: Gumino
g-gumino.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-gumino.summary: Radio Okapi reported that fighting resumed in the Minembwe Hauts Plateaux between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and the coalition of the armed groups Twirwaneho and Gumino, and, according to the Fizi territory administrator, that the FARDC supported by Wazalendo militiamen launched an assault on the coalition's positions. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q1-016"></sup> SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimonies, that clashes had intensified since Friday 3 April 2026 in the Bijombo area of Uvira territory between FARDC supported by FDNB elements, Wazalendo and Gumino fighters on one side and Twirwaneho fighters affiliated with the M23 on the other, displacing thousands of civilians; Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango and Kajembwe were among the most affected localities. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q2-009"></sup>

o-twangiza-mining-sa.name: Twangiza Mining SA
o-twangiza-mining-sa.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
o-twangiza-mining-sa.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that Twangiza Mining SA publicly denounced the systematic looting and destruction of industrial and environmental assets by AFC/M23, alleging active RDF support; Reuters also reported on 21 September 2025 the company's allegation that at least 500 kilograms of bullion had been looted since May. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-025"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 May 2025 AFC/M23 took over the industrial open-pit Twangiza gold mine, owned by Twangiza Mining SA, in Luhwindja chiefdom, Mwenga territory. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-022"></sup>

g-fdcc.name: FDCC
g-fdcc.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: the cited report)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post quoted a Wazalendo spokesperson in the area as saying that on the morning of Tuesday 4 November 2025 intense fighting broke out around Mikenge between Wazalendo of the FDCC of General Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin and 'the enemies of the AFC Twitwaneho M23, Red Tabara FNL ZABAMPEMA', and that the Wazalendo had already occupied a large part of Mikenge, including its stadium, and all of Bilalombili had fallen.

g-fdcc.summary: A Wazalendo spokesperson told Kivu Morning Post that Wazalendo of the FDCC, led by General Kakobanya, attacked AFC Twirwaneho M23 strongholds at Bijabo, Namara and Kamombo in Balala Nord groupement, Fizi territory, from Tuesday 1 July 2025. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q3-002"></sup> Kivu Morning Post quoted a Wazalendo spokesperson in the area as saying that on the morning of Tuesday 4 November 2025 intense fighting broke out around Mikenge between Wazalendo of the FDCC of General Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin and 'the enemies of the AFC Twitwaneho M23, Red Tabara FNL ZABAMPEMA', and that the Wazalendo had already occupied a large part of Mikenge, including its stadium, and all of Bilalombili had fallen. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q4-013"></sup>

g-mdlc-rradrdc.name: MDLC/RRADRDC
g-mdlc-rradrdc.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-mdlc-rradrdc.summary: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting broke out on Wednesday 30 July in Kamakombe village (Kabare territory) between M23-AFC rebels, described as allied to the RDF, and a Wazalendo group; it said the clashes had begun on the Tuesday in Mbayo village (Bugorhe groupement) following a reinforcement of M23 troops coming from Kavumu airport, and, according to several local sources, these troops launched an offensive against the Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC/RRADRDC), a Wazalendo branch present in the area. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2025Q3-004"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that four civilians were killed on Thursday 7 August in fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo of the MDLC group at Kasheke village, on the border of Kabare and Kalehe territories; according to local sources, the M23 attacked MDLC positions at Kamakombe and opened a second front against the MDLC headquarters at Kasheke, headed by the self-proclaimed general Imani Shabani, and the toll was described as provisional. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2025Q3-006"></sup>

o-government-of-burundi.name: Government of Burundi
o-government-of-burundi.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that security concerns led Burundi to close border posts with the DRC and designate several frontier areas as 'military zones' on 9 December 2025, and that on 25 February 2026 Burundi reopened a number of crossings.

o-government-of-burundi.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that security concerns led Burundi to close border posts with the DRC and designate several frontier areas as 'military zones' on 9 December 2025, and that on 25 February 2026 Burundi reopened a number of crossings. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-BI-FDLR-029"></sup> Anadolu reported that Burundi's Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned on Monday that 'any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q4-020"></sup>

g-rad.name: RAD
g-rad.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that in April 2025 the national defence minister had announced at Uvira that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city now depended exclusively on the national coordinator of the Réserve armée de défense (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.

Kivu Morning Post reported that at the MPDP launch the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander while insisting on discipline and respect for the laws of the Republic, and symbolically handed a weapon to commander Pascal Biriho as a sign of support.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the RAD provincial coordinator, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, announced on Thursday 22 January 2026 security measures for Uvira: at a press conference he formally banned carrying firearms and bladed weapons in urban areas and the erection of illegal roadblocks by self-defence groups, demanded the immediate withdrawal of the Wazalendo from the city centre, and said that urban security now fell exclusively under the PNC and the Military Police; the outlet added that the RAD was setting up a special unit to secure the city.

Tumaini Africa News reported that the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, accompanied by representatives of the VDP Wazalendo, expressed gratitude to President Tshisekedi and the central government for a 325 US dollar incentive payment called 'effort de guerre', in a press briefing held in Kalundu commune, Uvira city.

g-rad.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that at the MPDP launch the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander while insisting on discipline and respect for the laws of the Republic, and symbolically handed a weapon to commander Pascal Biriho as a sign of support. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-003"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that Lungele Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society coordination framework, cited an incident on 12 March in which Dodos Ngama, a young man of 30, was "fusillé" (shot) by a "VDP -RAD Wazalendo" element at Ilinda, and said that on 13 March Mukaba Masilia Ndebo, aged 56, was also "fusillé" at "Kibumb a" (spelling as printed). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKC-2026H1-011"></sup>

o-sadc.name: SADC
o-sadc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
o-sadc.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that the SADC stated in an official communiqué that 'SAMIDRC has not participated in any joint operations' and refuted AFC/M23's allegations, which it qualified as 'inaccurate and misleading'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-039"></sup> Rwanda's foreign ministry said on 2 February 2025 that it rejected the accusations against the Rwanda Defence Force made in the statement of the SADC extraordinary summit of 31 January 2025, and said the RDF does not attack civilians. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q1-009"></sup>

o-societe-civile-plurielle-et-forces-viv.name: Societe civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu
o-societe-civile-plurielle-et-forces-viv.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
o-societe-civile-plurielle-et-forces-viv.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23, attended by AFC/M23 officials including Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2026-025"></sup> Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete, Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs, AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data, affirmed that it did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; further meetings in late March and April 2026 resulted in an agreement that only aggregate data on sexual violence would be shared. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2026-025"></sup>

g-updc.name: UPDC
g-updc.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-updc.summary: Radio Okapi reported that local sources denounced extortion of residents of Ufamandu 2 by fighters of the group Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, 'd'un certain Noah Maachano', who were said to be imposing since the previous week a parallel tax of 10 000 Congolese francs (3.5 USD) per household. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2025H1-018"></sup>

g-uhuru.name: Uhuru
g-uhuru.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily.

g-uhuru.summary: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-003"></sup> Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Kasopo locality (Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi) was deserted after two days of fighting from Wednesday 10 September between M23 rebels and a coalition of Wazalendo groups made up of elements of the MAC, the APCLS and Uhuru. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2025H2-008"></sup>

u-satan-ii.name: Satan II
u-satan-ii.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission)

timeline.text: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting.

u-satan-ii.summary: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2025-012"></sup> The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that during their retreat soldiers from the 'Satan II' and 'Guépard' units repeatedly entered homes, looted property and raped civilians, following a consistent pattern across multiple locations and over a wide geographic area. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-HRC-026"></sup>

o-anr.name: ANR
o-anr.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: ReliefWeb, republishing a MONUSCO item,)
o-anr.summary: ReliefWeb, republishing a MONUSCO item, reported that BCNUDH said in a press release that 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented last year, affecting 1 534 victims (854 women and 672 girls), that North and South Kivu concentrate nearly 80 per cent of documented victims, that armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of victims, with M23 first with 439 victims, and that FARDC, PNC and ANR members were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2026-022"></sup> Amnesty International reported that M23 detention sites in Bukavu were the main ANR office and a military camp in the Bagira district; it said that at the time of publication it had received no response from representatives of the M23 (or from Rwanda's justice ministry and prosecutor general). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2025Q2-022"></sup>

g-codeco.name: CODECO
g-codeco.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Secretary-General)
g-codeco.summary: The UN Secretary-General reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office documented 1,359 human rights violations and abuses nationwide in the reporting period, and that AFC/M23 remained the largest single perpetrator, responsible for 489 human rights abuses affecting 1,279 victims (752 men, 391 women, 125 children and 11 persons), followed by Wazalendo groups (143 abuses), ADF (98), FDLR (44) and CODECO (23). <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-001"></sup> The Group of Experts reported, for the 2025 cases verified by the UN, that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of victims (M23 ranked first, followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions) and State agents for 19 per cent (FARDC soldiers first, followed by the PNC), and that the UPDF, the FNDB and RED-Tabara were also responsible for CRSV cases. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-037"></sup>

g-ngumino.name: Ngumino
g-ngumino.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe.

g-ngumino.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-006"></sup>

o-ipis.name: IPIS
o-ipis.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: IPIS)
o-ipis.summary: IPIS reported that by late February 2026 the pro-government Wazalendo coalition launched a large-scale offensive on AFC/M23 positions in the Osso and Bahunde chiefdoms south of Masisi town, and, supported by FARDC air strikes, temporarily recaptured several villages including Chugi, Kibabi and Kaniro, which AFC/M23 quickly regained while retaining control of the coltan mines around Rubaya. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-018"></sup> IPIS reported that a source mentioned that ten women were allegedly executed in Shabunda territory for resisting Wazalendo demands for forced payments at mining-site entrances, 'jeton corporel' (body tokens) and invasive searches. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-016"></sup>

o-afjep.name: AFJEP
o-afjep.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-afjep.summary: Actualite.cd reported that a 32-year-old woman was raped and then killed by armed men on a date it gives as 'mardi le 13 juillet' in Kamituga, South Kivu, and that, according to civil-society sources, her body was found in the morning in the Kalinga quarter. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2026-014"></sup> The Association des femmes journalistes engagées pour la paix (AFJEP) said the rape was committed by unidentified persons and called for an investigation. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2026-014"></sup> Actualite.cd described Kamituga as controlled by Wazalendo militiamen allied to the national army ('alliés à l’armée congolaise'). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-2026-014"></sup>

o-mutualite-des-banyamulenge.name: Mutualité des Banyamulenge
o-mutualite-des-banyamulenge.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: SOS Médias Burundi)
o-mutualite-des-banyamulenge.summary: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced in a communiqué acts of discrimination, physical violence and intimidation, including women and girls beaten in Kabindula and denial of access to drinking water, some demonstrators saying 'Allez puiser au Rwanda'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q3-020"></sup> SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced the abduction of a FARDC soldier and a policeman, both Banyamulenge. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q3-021"></sup>

o-expanded-joint-verification-mechanism-.name: Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus
o-expanded-joint-verification-mechanism-.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Secretary-General)

timeline.text: The UN Secretary-General reported that, with MONUSCO support, the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus conducted its first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August 2026 and a second mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September.

o-expanded-joint-verification-mechanism-.summary: The UN Secretary-General reported that, with MONUSCO support, the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus conducted its first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August 2026 and a second mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UNDOCS-008"></sup>

o-csdf.name: CSDF
o-csdf.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: CSDF, a Congolese women's health and rights organisation,)
o-csdf.summary: CSDF, a Congolese women's health and rights organisation, said that June 2025 marked a notable deterioration in the security and human rights situation in Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories; that, according to protection monitoring data covering 22 health zones, 842 violations were documented; that serious incidents rose by more than 35 per cent compared with May, with Masisi alone accounting for 50 per cent of the cases, followed by Nyiragongo (21 per cent) and Rutshuru (12 per cent); and that June 2025 was the annual peak of gender-based violence, with 247 documented cases (17 per cent of all violations of the month), of which 93 per cent were rapes. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-NK-2025-006"></sup>

g-mai-mai-kifuafua.name: Maï-Maï Kifuafua
g-mai-mai-kifuafua.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a public declaration from Mbwavinywa, three armed groups announced their break with Kinshasa to join the M23/AFC: the FPP/AP of the self-proclaimed general Kabido, the NDC-R/M and Maï-Maï Kifuafua.

g-mai-mai-kifuafua.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a public declaration from Mbwavinywa, three armed groups announced their break with Kinshasa to join the M23/AFC: the FPP/AP of the self-proclaimed general Kabido, the NDC-R/M and Maï-Maï Kifuafua. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2025H1-009"></sup> Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that the M23 also controlled gold-bearing zones such as Musigha, in the Bunyatenge area of Lubero, forcing the self-proclaimed general Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido, leader of the FPP-AP group, to rally them to 'keep his mining interests'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-NKN-FRONT-008"></sup>

g-bana-bateseka.name: Bana Bateseka
g-bana-bateseka.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)
g-bana-bateseka.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that self-proclaimed general Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », was shot dead during fighting between his Wazalendo group and that of his rival Fiston Njoli at Butembo, according to Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, president of the communal civil society; the fighting began on a Sunday morning on Munzambaye hill, Vulamba commune, and lasted until Monday 5 January, and the body was reportedly displayed publicly at Furu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019"></sup>

g-far-west.name: Far West (Wazalendo movement)
g-far-west.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-far-west.summary: Radio Okapi reported that a member of the Wazalendo movement called « Far West » was sentenced to death on Wednesday 6 May, the Butembo garrison military tribunal having found him guilty of the murder of a motorcyclist and of the rape followed by murder of his female customer, facts which occurred the previous week at Kimbulu, Lubero territory; Lubero civil society also demanded the outright abolition of the « Far West » movement, which it accuses of being involved in serious human rights violations. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-010"></sup> Enquete.cd reported, citing several local sources, that Wazalendo movement leader James Fyeka Adui, arrested in Uvira on 5 September, had been transferred to Kinshasa some days earlier, and that he is accused, according to concordant sources, of involvement in the murder of a civilian in Uvira in May 2026; the outlet added that these accusations had not yet been publicly confirmed in detail by judicial authorities. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-030"></sup>

u-21st-principal-defence-brigade.name: 21st principal defence brigade (FARDC)
u-21st-principal-defence-brigade.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain, and that the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition continued to contest AFC/M23 and RDF advances on multiple fronts.

The UN Group of Experts assessed that control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens the influence of AFC/M23 over the northern 'gate' of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.

The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting.

The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.
The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF took Bukavu on 16 February, Government authorities, FDNB and FARDC withdrew towards Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura in Burundi.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, to restore security, the FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu governorate were relocated to Uvira in early March, and that in early April DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and former RAD national coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to appease the Wazalendo groups.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its report, relations between FARDC and Wazalendo had improved and some Wazalendo groups had left the centre of Uvira at the request of FARDC command.

The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its final report, the AFC/M23 controlled mining areas in Kalehe, Walungu and Mwenga territories as far as Kamanyola in the south, while the FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo kept control of the Ruzizi plain and held positions along the Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira road, blocking the AFC/M23 advance towards Uvira.

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.

The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.

The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.

The UN Secretary-General reported that in South Kivu, Twirwaneho and M23 pushed back FARDC outside of the general Minembwe area and regained control of Point Zero on 4 July, effectively restoring the frontline to its late January 2026 configuration.

u-21st-principal-defence-brigade.summary: The report of the UN Human Rights Council fact-finding mission stated that sources specifically identified members of the 'Guépard' and 'Satan II' FARDC units, deployed along the South Kivu frontline, as responsible for multiple incidents of sexual violence and looting. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SV-2025-012"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-017"></sup>

g-uplc.name: UPLC (Germain Kambale Mayani)
g-uplc.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-uplc.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that, with FARDC counter-offensive operations affected by troop shortages, FARDC relied increasingly on Wazalendo armed groups against ADF, including the UPLC led by "General" Germain Kambale Mayani, elements of the NDC-R of sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, and a local APCLS detachment led by "General" Fimbo. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-010"></sup> The Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups established new geographically organized coalitions called 'synergies': the 'Synergie Front Grand Nord' (24 armed groups in Lubero and Beni, commanded by UPLC leader 'General' Mayani), the 'Synergie Petit Nord' (14 groups in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo, commanded by Jonas Bigabo), and the 'Synergie Masisi-Walikale' (17 groups, led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-042"></sup>

o-beni-garrison-military-tribunal.name: Beni garrison military tribunal
o-beni-garrison-military-tribunal.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Delivered a verdict at Manyama-Beu against two soldiers; hearings for a third soldier prosecuted for alleged rape were suspended

o-beni-garrison-military-tribunal.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the Beni garrison military tribunal (North Kivu) sentenced three FARDC officers (two lieutenants and a captain) to death for desertion and breach of orders, after they had been recruited, according to the court, by a man presenting himself as coordinator of the Comité national des patriotes (CONAP); two men presenting themselves as Wazalendo commanders got twenty years in prison for, notably, illegally recruiting soldiers and spreading false information, having set up, according to military justice, a clandestine recruitment network in the Malepe quarter of Beni using without mandate the name of the Réserve armée de la défense (RAD); the verdict came on the evening of Friday 10 July. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009"></sup>

g-kaganga.name: Kaganga (MDPC group)
g-kaganga.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni)
g-kaganga.summary: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the 'kapita' Kombi Lwayivweka, 38, was arrested by presumed Wazalendu of the MDPC group of general Kaganga for not bringing food to the fighters, taken to their camp, tortured and whipped, and released on Tuesday 22 September after local authorities intervened; according to the radio's sources his release was obtained for payment of USD 50 and a hen. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2026H2-010"></sup>

o-afc-m23-health-crisis-cell.name: AFC/M23 health crisis cell
o-afc-m23-health-crisis-cell.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Enquête.cd)
o-afc-m23-health-crisis-cell.summary: Enquête.cd reported that the health crisis cell set up by the rebel administration announced on Thursday 3 September a new confirmed Ebola case in the Kayna health zone, a 21-year-old man from Butembo identified at a health checkpoint in the Itsu health area and transferred to the Kirumba quarantine site; it said Reuters also reported on 4 September a new case in an AFC/M23-controlled zone after the epidemic had been declared over in the territories under its control. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2026Q3-010"></sup>

g-mai-mai-group-of-le-blanc.name: Maï-Maï group of "Le Blanc"
g-mai-mai-group-of-le-blanc.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-mai-mai-group-of-le-blanc.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC and the Ugandan army (UPDF) retook control of Muhola hill in Baswagha chiefdom on Friday 4 July, described as a stronghold of a Maï-Maï group led by a commander nicknamed « Le Blanc », a week after intense fighting. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKN-2025H2-002"></sup>

o-kitsamba-clpc.name: Kitsamba / CLPC
o-kitsamba-clpc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Kivu Morning Post)
o-kitsamba-clpc.summary: The Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 54 people were killed in attacks by ADF-MTM since January 2026 in the Baswagha chiefdom and the Bapere sector of Lubero territory, according to a provisional toll compiled on Thursday by the Comité local de protection communautaire (CLPC), whose president Vianney Kitsamba cited 33 deaths in Baswagha and 21 civilians in the Bapere sector. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-010"></sup>

u-m23-1st-battalion-1st-brigade.name: M23 1st Battalion, 1st Brigade
u-m23-1st-battalion-1st-brigade.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Human Rights Watch)

timeline.text: Human Rights Watch said its research indicates the M23 military operations in Binza in July 2025 were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Col. Samuel Mushagara and Brig. Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions.

u-m23-1st-battalion-1st-brigade.summary: Human Rights Watch said its research indicates the M23 military operations in Binza in July 2025 were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Col. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-002"></sup> Samuel Mushagara and Brig. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-002"></sup> Gen. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-002"></sup> Baudoin Ngaruye, respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-002"></sup>

u-afc-m23-fourth-brigade.name: AFC/M23 Fourth Brigade
u-afc-m23-fourth-brigade.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The Group of Experts reported that in Bwito chiefdom AFC/M23 deployed its newly constituted 'Fourth Brigade', reportedly composed of recent recruits including former Wazalendo and FARDC elements, under the command of Mapenzi, the former leader of NDC-R/M who joined AFC/M23 in March 2025, replacing RDF forces partially redeployed from the area since September.

u-afc-m23-fourth-brigade.summary: The Group of Experts reported that in Bwito chiefdom AFC/M23 deployed its newly constituted 'Fourth Brigade', reportedly composed of recent recruits including former Wazalendo and FARDC elements, under the command of Mapenzi, the former leader of NDC-R/M who joined AFC/M23 in March 2025, replacing RDF forces partially redeployed from the area since September. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-087"></sup>

o-north-kivu-provincial-youth-council.name: North Kivu provincial youth council
o-north-kivu-provincial-youth-council.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-north-kivu-provincial-youth-council.summary: Actualite.cd reported that a report by the North Kivu provincial youth council documented 47 deaths, 75 cases of sexual violence, 14 abductions, 66 armed robberies and 63 cases of arson between 7 June and 3 July 2025 in Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories and Goma city. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-015"></sup>

o-heal-africa-hospital.name: Heal Africa hospital
o-heal-africa-hospital.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)
o-heal-africa-hospital.summary: The Group of Experts reported that in an interview excerpt published on X on 13 March 2025, 'General' Sultani Makenga, asked about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, repeated that the men arrested were former FARDC pretending to be patients or hospital staff. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-059"></sup> The EastAfrican reported that the AFC (Congo River Alliance) 'strongly denies' the UN human rights office's allegations of attacks on hospitals, saying it never targeted civilian establishments, that the UN mission MONUSCO had manipulated the details, and that its raid was aimed at securing medical infrastructure it said had been infiltrated by fighters; the AFC claimed the heads of the hospitals corroborated in the operation. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-HC-NK-2025-020"></sup>

g-pareco.name: PARECO
g-pareco.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Named by Rwanda's representative as a recipient of ammunition and food airlifted to Ntoto

g-pareco.summary: Radio Okapi reported that despite a ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, fighting continued between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said that since early Friday 20 February AFC/M23 had been fighting Wazalendo of PARECO at Mitimingi, Kaunda and Mbiso in Masisi territory, and that other clashes were reported in some areas of Rutshuru territory. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2026Q1-010"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that, despite the ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, clashes continued in eastern DRC between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said the truce had been proposed on 11 February by Angola after a meeting in Luanda, and that the DRC officially adhered to it while AFC/M23 had committed to an immediate halt to hostilities under the Doha process. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-MED-2026-018"></sup>

u-direction-pour-la-securite-et-les-rens.name: Direction pour la securite et les renseignements (DSR)
u-direction-pour-la-securite-et-les-rens.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Congovirtuel)

timeline.text: Congovirtuel reported, citing Africa Intelligence, that Théo Binamungu, described as a close political adviser to Nangaa, was arrested at the end of August by loyalists of Makenga, interrogated by the military intelligence of the Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) and then by the Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), and transferred to Munzenze central prison on 8 September.

u-direction-pour-la-securite-et-les-rens.summary: Congovirtuel reported, citing Africa Intelligence, that Théo Binamungu, described as a close political adviser to Nangaa, was arrested at the end of August by loyalists of Makenga, interrogated by the military intelligence of the Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) and then by the Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), and transferred to Munzenze central prison on 8 September. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2026Q3-013"></sup>

o-unicef.name: UNICEF
o-unicef.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: UN News)
o-unicef.summary: UN News, citing a MONUSCO press release, reported that a French UNICEF employee was killed on Wednesday 11 March 2026 in a drone attack on a building housing humanitarian workers in Goma, and that the attack also killed two civilians and damaged civilian homes. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-003"></sup> Beto.cd, in an article credited to AFP summarising the UN Group of Experts report S/2026/466, reported that the experts reconstructed the strike that killed UNICEF worker Karine Buisset in Goma on 11 March as an aerial fragmentation munition fired by a drone coming from Lake Kivu, and that attribution remains contested. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-004"></sup>

o-reporters-sans-frontieres.name: Reporters sans frontieres (RSF)
o-reporters-sans-frontieres.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-reporters-sans-frontieres.summary: Actualite.cd, relaying Reporters sans frontières (RSF), reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was held in a container at the North Kivu Provincial Assembly in Goma by the AFC/M23, forced to film an interview of the M23 spokesperson and then released, according to RSF on Friday 24 April. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-018"></sup>

o-iccn.name: ICCN
o-iccn.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-iccn.summary: Radio Okapi reported on Monday 25 May that aerial strikes attributed to military drones, whose origin remained undetermined and which no party had claimed, hit Rubaya (Masisi) and Rumangabo (Rutshuru) the day before; a strike on Sunday around 07:30 hit a training centre for the women and widows of ICCN rangers in the Virunga National Park compound at Rumangabo, with no loss of life confirmed, and an earlier strike around 00:15 targeted a guest house in Rubaya. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-006"></sup>

o-african-union.name: African Union
o-african-union.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Top Africa News)

timeline.text: Top Africa News reported that African Union facilitators held closed-door talks with AFC/M23 leaders in Goma on Monday, meeting political coordinator Corneille Nangaa and his deputies Bertrand Bisimwa and Freddy Kaniki; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement received the mission in the framework of efforts toward a political, durable and African-led resolution of the conflict, and no joint communiqué or concrete agreements were announced.

o-african-union.summary: Top Africa News reported that African Union facilitators held closed-door talks with AFC/M23 leaders in Goma on Monday, meeting political coordinator Corneille Nangaa and his deputies Bertrand Bisimwa and Freddy Kaniki; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement received the mission in the framework of efforts toward a political, durable and African-led resolution of the conflict, and no joint communiqué or concrete agreements were announced. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2026Q4-008"></sup> Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa called on Burundian President and African Union chair Évariste Ndayishimiye to guarantee humanitarian access to the Minembwe highlands, denouncing what he called a 'blocus humanitaire' affecting the mostly Banyamulenge Tutsi zone. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-M23-2026-015"></sup>

o-karisimbi-communal-youth-council.name: Karisimbi communal youth council
o-karisimbi-communal-youth-council.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: MediaCongo)
o-karisimbi-communal-youth-council.summary: MediaCongo reported that the Karisimbi communal youth council alerted on Wednesday 8 July 2026 to the abduction of more than 50 young people by armed men in the Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters of Goma, and that the council fears their possible forced enrolment into the March 23 movement (M23/AFC). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-016"></sup>

o-north-kivu-provincial-health-inspectio.name: North Kivu Provincial Health Inspection Department (IPS)
o-north-kivu-provincial-health-inspectio.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)
o-north-kivu-provincial-health-inspectio.summary: The Group of Experts reported that IPS inspectors of the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department inspected the premises of humanitarian actors after an 11 February 2026 AFC/M23 'Note Explicative', requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits to curb what AFC/M23 alleged were 'fake' victims. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-031"></sup>

g-cmpdn.name: CMPDN
g-cmpdn.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-cmpdn.summary: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 19 January 2025 the FARDC, supported by FDLR combatants and the Coalition of Patriotic Movements for the Defense of the Nation (CMPDN), attacked AFC/M23 in Masisi centre. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-041"></sup>

g-fcr.name: FCR
g-fcr.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The FARDC, in a communiqué)

timeline.text: The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies.

g-fcr.summary: The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-CMD-001"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that on 7 March 2025 'General' Kasereka Kasyano Kabidon announced the allegiance of the Front commun de la résistance (FCR), a Wazalendo coalition, to AFC/M23, but several FCR members disavowed the announcement and reiterated their loyalty to the Government. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-033"></sup>

o-alphamin-bisie-mining.name: Alphamin Bisie Mining
o-alphamin-bisie-mining.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-alphamin-bisie-mining.summary: Actualite.cd reported that the company Alphamin Bisie Mining (ABM) announced the immediate suspension of its mining operations from Friday 14 March because of growing risks to the safety of its staff. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-NKW-MASISI-005"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that further military advances towards Uvira resulted in the paralysis of mining activities in Kamanyola, and that the Alphamin Bisie tin mine in Walikale territory suspended operations from 13 March to mid-April 2025. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-048"></sup>

o-msf-holland.name: MSF Holland
o-msf-holland.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-msf-holland.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing witnesses, that Walikale's general hospital and an NGO logistics base were damaged during the fighting, causing deaths and injuries, after the Walikale area passed under rebel occupation. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2025H1-006"></sup>

o-ocean-heights-aviation-training-centre.name: Ocean Heights Aviation Training Centre
o-ocean-heights-aviation-training-centre.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
o-ocean-heights-aviation-training-centre.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that it identified the aircraft destroyed by a FARDC airstrike on 27 March 2025 at the Kigoma airfield in Walikale, then under AFC/M23 control, as a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan operated by Ocean Heights Aviation Training Centre, a company based in Entebbe, Uganda. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-045"></sup>

g-mac.name: MAC
g-mac.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-mac.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Kasopo locality (Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi) was deserted after two days of fighting from Wednesday 10 September between M23 rebels and a coalition of Wazalendo groups made up of elements of the MAC, the APCLS and Uhuru. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2025H2-008"></sup>

o-war-child.name: War Child
o-war-child.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
o-war-child.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 January 2026 a drone strike hit the office of the INGO War Child in Masisi, killing seven people and injuring 42 and others, mainly women and children, and said it is continuing to investigate; in the main text it listed the strike, which it says hit the War Child sub-base in Masisi centre, among FARDC drone operations that affected civilian objects and populations. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-007"></sup> Actualite.cd reported, in an article on the Forum des ONGI en RDC condemning drone strikes in Goma, that in January 2026 the office of the international organisation War Child in Masisi, North Kivu, had already suffered significant damage following an air attack in the area. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-LOCAL-015"></sup>

g-kalomendo.name: Kalomendo
g-kalomendo.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily.

g-kalomendo.summary: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-003"></sup>

u-sokola-1-grand-nord.name: Sokola 1 Grand-Nord
u-sokola-1-grand-nord.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: 7sur7.cd)
u-sokola-1-grand-nord.summary: 7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of operational sector Sokola 1 Grand-Nord and Front Nord, said on 20 September they observe the ceasefire on all North Kivu front lines while denouncing attacks they attribute to AFC/M23-RDF on the Walikale-Masisi axis, which they said violate the Doha and Washington accords and cause displacement toward Walikale, with villages burned and fields destroyed. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-014"></sup>

o-cfr-rdc.name: CFR RDC
o-cfr-rdc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-cfr-rdc.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the Club des Filles Reporters RDC (CFR RDC), after a mission from 25 to 27 September 2026, said nearly 2 350 displaced families lived in precarious conditions at Lukaraba (Walikale) and Hombo Sud (Kalehe, South Kivu); at Lukaraba the families had fled Ziralo, Ufamandu, Remeka, Lurere and Biriko, and at Hombo Sud the hospital was said to be under strain from sick or war-wounded displaced people. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKW-2026H2-018"></sup>

u-police-militaire.name: Police militaire
u-police-militaire.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
u-police-militaire.summary: Radio Okapi reported that, according to major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, the defendants were arrested on 20 October following incidents at Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, on the border with Masisi territory, which left two dead, a soldier and a civilian; the page says the facts allegedly occurred during an altercation between the soldiers and Military Police elements trying to stop them from leaving the combat zone without authorisation. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004"></sup>

u-3415e-regiment.name: 3415e régiment
u-3415e-regiment.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Ten soldiers of the regiment sentenced by the Goma garrison military tribunal for the murder of their company commander

u-3415e-regiment.summary: Radio Okapi reported that fifty-four soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC had been appearing since Monday 26 October before the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, North Kivu, prosecuted notably for murder, abandoning post, dissipation of war munitions and refusal to obey. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-003"></sup>

o-tribunal-militaire-de-garnison-de-goma.name: tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma
o-tribunal-militaire-de-garnison-de-goma.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Sentenced six people at a circuit hearing in Walikale, including a VDP fighter prosecuted for rape who received 20 years
Sentenced Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre to death for murder at a circuit chamber in Walikale
Sentenced ten FARDC soldiers of the 3415th regiment at Walikale-centre

o-tribunal-militaire-de-garnison-de-goma.summary: Radio Okapi reported that fifty-four soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC had been appearing since Monday 26 October before the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, North Kivu, prosecuted notably for murder, abandoning post, dissipation of war munitions and refusal to obey. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-003"></sup>

g-adf-iscap.name: ADF-ISCAP
g-adf-iscap.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-adf-iscap.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that it received information about, but was not able to investigate, new cases of conflict-related sexual violence in Ituri and North Kivu, in particular sexual slavery and forced pregnancy by ADF-ISCAP elements leading to the birth of children. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-005"></sup>

o-coalition-pamoja-kwa-amani.name: Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani
o-coalition-pamoja-kwa-amani.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani)

timeline.text: Denounced the summary execution of two young men of one family at Kaniola, Walungu territory, attributed to AFC/M23 elements
Said at least 12 people were arrested and summarily executed in Katana groupement by AFC/M23 rebels

o-coalition-pamoja-kwa-amani.summary: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that the AFC-M23 rebels had issued a communiqué asking Burundi to withdraw its forces and proposing the opening of a humanitarian corridor to facilitate their return. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q4-023"></sup> The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that Burundi had affirmed its will to keep its troops on Congolese soil and to continue operations alongside the FARDC, in line with the bilateral partnership, according to its foreign minister, Édouard BIZIMANA. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q4-024"></sup>

g-alliance-des-nationalistes-congolais-p.name: Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains
g-alliance-des-nationalistes-congolais-p.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-alliance-des-nationalistes-congolais-p.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported, in a paragraph on abuses by VDP/Wazalendo groups, that Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains combatants have been implicated most frequently in serious abuses against civilians, such as abductions, lootings, rape, unlawful killings and arson. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-036"></sup>

g-burundian-police.name: Burundian police
g-burundian-police.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Human Rights Watch)
g-burundian-police.summary: Human Rights Watch reported that in Burundi on 8 September 2025 police and ruling-party youths detained hundreds of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers, according to several witnesses and media reports, giving them the 'choice' of going to an official camp or returning to Congo, which about 80 people did. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UV-CTRL-005"></sup>

o-ministry-of-defence-of-the-drc.name: Ministry of Defence of the DRC
o-ministry-of-defence-of-the-drc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that the DRC Ministry of Defence announced on 29 January 2025 that, by presidential order of Tuesday 28 January, general-major Evariste Somo Kakule was appointed military governor of North Kivu province under the state of siege.

o-ministry-of-defence-of-the-drc.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the DRC Ministry of Defence announced on 29 January 2025 that, by presidential order of Tuesday 28 January, general-major Evariste Somo Kakule was appointed military governor of North Kivu province under the state of siege. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-FARDC-001"></sup>

o-protection-cluster.name: Protection Cluster
o-protection-cluster.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: In its July 2025 protection highlights, the DRC Protection Cluster)
o-protection-cluster.summary: In its July 2025 protection highlights, the DRC Protection Cluster reported, for Mwenga territory, where armed groups were committing extortion and other abuses notably in Itombwe sector, that at least 05 cases of rape and several acts of extortion, beatings and abductions had reportedly been alleged at the start of the period, in a context of retreat of government forces and extension of armed groups' hold over localities of the territory. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q3-017"></sup>

o-cre-seko.name: CRE SEKO
o-cre-seko.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-cre-seko.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that a mixed unit of police and FARDC soldiers dispersed a peaceful march in Kamituga on Tuesday 22 July against electricity overbilling by the company CRE SEKO, with live fire and tear gas reported and several arrests; organiser Lucky Mutiki said the movement would continue. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKC-2025H2-025"></sup>

g-mai-mai-corbeau.name: Mai Mai Corbeau
g-mai-mai-corbeau.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-mai-mai-corbeau.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early September competition over the control of roadblocks in Mwenga sparked violence among Wazalendo groups, notably Mai Mai Corbeau and Mai Mai Malaika, which forced the FARDC to intervene to dismantle the growing number of barriers. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-038"></sup>

g-mai-mai-malaika.name: Mai Mai Malaika
g-mai-mai-malaika.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
g-mai-mai-malaika.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early September competition over the control of roadblocks in Mwenga sparked violence among Wazalendo groups, notably Mai Mai Corbeau and Mai Mai Malaika, which forced the FARDC to intervene to dismantle the growing number of barriers. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-038"></sup>

o-obapg.name: OBAPG
o-obapg.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-obapg.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the citizens' movement OBAPG said the latest reported attack on the Bukavu-Walungu-Mwenga road occurred at Kankinda, where several traders were robbed of their goods and women were reportedly victims of sexual violence. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKC-2026H2-008"></sup>

g-mcdpn.name: MCDPN
g-mcdpn.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 9 April Wazalendo of COPACO and MCDPN, commanded by self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho, Maike and Bahige, recovered Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 and Nyawaronga on the Kalehe highlands after fighting with M23 backed by Rwanda.

g-mcdpn.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 9 April Wazalendo of COPACO and MCDPN, commanded by self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho, Maike and Bahige, recovered Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 and Nyawaronga on the Kalehe highlands after fighting with M23 backed by Rwanda. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2025Q2-001"></sup>

o-south-kivu-provincial-government.name: South Kivu provincial government
o-south-kivu-provincial-government.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that political-administrative authorities, FARDC soldiers and police settled in the city of Uvira on Monday 24 February, and that governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi, his deputy and about 600 uniformed men, including police and soldiers, who had left Bukavu some days earlier for Burundi, arrived in Uvira through the Kavimvira border.

The Group of Experts reported that after the Wazalendo return to Uvira in January 2026 the South Kivu Governor convened all Wazalendo leaders, banned unauthorized armed elements, roadblocks and any substitution for government functions, and arrested recalcitrant combatants, and that provincial authorities began a registration process with payment of $325 to each registered combatant.

o-south-kivu-provincial-government.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the South Kivu provincial government spokesperson, Me Luganywa-Bashizi Didier, condemned the abuses reported at Kaniola and called for those responsible to be brought to justice. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-DRC-2026-014"></sup> SOS Médias Burundi reported that the spokesperson of the South Kivu provincial government, Luganywa Bashizi Didier Kabi, relayed the position of governor Jean Jacques Purusi, who condemned the oral and physical violence of the previous two days in certain quarters of Uvira. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q3-007"></sup>

g-mcdpin.name: MCDPIN
g-mcdpin.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)

timeline.text: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye.

Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local civil society, that Wazalendo of the MCDPIN group of 'Monsieur Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik' and of 'Monsieur Grevisse Nsimparinga' systematically looted civilians' property at Chambombo, a village of Nyalugusha in Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe, on Monday 13 April 2026.

g-mcdpin.summary: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2026Q2-002"></sup>

g-mai-mai-lamuka.name: Maï-Maï Lamuka
g-mai-mai-lamuka.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)

timeline.text: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, Wazalendo fighters led by Noah Maachano, of the Maï-Maï Lamuka group, had reportedly also deployed in several neighbouring villages, notably Shangi, Katahandwa and Shoa.

g-mai-mai-lamuka.summary: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, Wazalendo fighters led by Noah Maachano, of the Maï-Maï Lamuka group, had reportedly also deployed in several neighbouring villages, notably Shangi, Katahandwa and Shoa. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKN-2026Q3-008"></sup> Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that fighting between Wazalendo armed groups and AFC/M23 rebels was reported on Wednesday 10 June in Masisi territory, notably at Kishanja and Kasenyi, with heavy and light weapons heard. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ATR-NK-2026-008"></sup>

g-rushaba-wazalendo-group.name: Rushaba wazalendo group
g-rushaba-wazalendo-group.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
