timeline.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23.

Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said Rushaba had been with Nyamusaraba in the 'Task force' together with the Burundian forces before deserting it, starting clashes at Kashama and allying with the M23. The article describes the Task force as composed of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo, and quotes another source on site as saying there was a coalition of Banyamulenge based in Kahololo/Marungu, Rushaba wazalendo and M23 elements from Kaziba.

g-rushaba-wazalendo-group.summary: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q1-030"></sup>

g-ngomazito-elements.name: Ngomazito elements
g-ngomazito-elements.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)
g-ngomazito-elements.summary: The Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with the FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain: FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover, and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-046"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain; for example FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-BI-FDLR-026"></sup>

g-kamama.name: Kamama (Wazalendo group)
g-kamama.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)

timeline.text: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23.

Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said Rushaba had been with Nyamusaraba in the 'Task force' together with the Burundian forces before deserting it, starting clashes at Kashama and allying with the M23. The article describes the Task force as composed of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo, and quotes another source on site as saying there was a coalition of Banyamulenge based in Kahololo/Marungu, Rushaba wazalendo and M23 elements from Kaziba.

Kivu Morning Post reported that self-proclaimed general Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », was shot dead during fighting between his Wazalendo group and that of his rival Fiston Njoli at Butembo, according to Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, president of the communal civil society; the fighting began on a Sunday morning on Munzambaye hill, Vulamba commune, and lasted until Monday 5 January, and the body was reportedly displayed publicly at Furu.

g-kamama.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that self-proclaimed general Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », was shot dead during fighting between his Wazalendo group and that of his rival Fiston Njoli at Butembo, according to Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, president of the communal civil society; the fighting began on a Sunday morning on Munzambaye hill, Vulamba commune, and lasted until Monday 5 January, and the body was reportedly displayed publicly at Furu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q1-030"></sup>

g-ebuela-kibukila.name: Ebuela / Kibukila (Mai-Mai)
g-ebuela-kibukila.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Group of Experts)
g-ebuela-kibukila.summary: The Group of Experts reported, for the 2025 cases verified by the UN, that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of victims (M23 ranked first, followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions) and State agents for 19 per cent (FARDC soldiers first, followed by the PNC), and that the UPDF, the FNDB and RED-Tabara were also responsible for CRSV cases. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-037"></sup> Ebuteli reported that on 29 January the Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara coalition and the FNL attacked the Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo in the villages of Kilumbi and Abala in Fizi territory, killing three Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-047"></sup>

u-22e-task-force.name: 22e Task Force (TAFOK)
u-22e-task-force.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: CongoRassure)
u-22e-task-force.summary: CongoRassure reported that a new battalion, the '22ᵉ Task Force (TAFOK)', was being mobilised in the border town of Gatumba before deployment to Bukavu, bringing the total of Burundian battalions in the DRC to sixteen, five of them positioned in the Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira to hunt Burundian rebels; that the Burundian regiment was under the command of 'général Pontien Hakizimana, alias Mingi' and structured in four brigades of three battalions each; and that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10 000 soldiers, a strength currently fluctuating between 8 000 and 12 000. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-001"></sup>

u-task-force-congo.name: Task Force Congo (TAFOC)
u-task-force-congo.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 approximately 14 FDNB battalions under the 'Task Force Congo' (TAFOC) umbrella were still on DRC territory, of which 10 were reportedly in the Ruzizi Plain, two in and around Uvira and two in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu.

u-task-force-congo.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 approximately 14 FDNB battalions under the 'Task Force Congo' (TAFOC) umbrella were still on DRC territory, of which 10 were reportedly in the Ruzizi Plain, two in and around Uvira and two in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q2-021"></sup>

u-m23-headquarters-regiment.name: M23 Headquarters Regiment
u-m23-headquarters-regiment.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026))
u-m23-headquarters-regiment.summary: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, the M23 Headquarters Regiment as now deployed to South Kivu, with its 1st battalion deployed in the Uvira operation and its 2nd battalion deployed to Minembwe. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-028"></sup> The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Colonel Kamanzi Rubens (“Romeo Kilo”) as commander of the Headquarters Regiment (now deployed to South Kivu), Lt Col “Romeo Delta” as commander of its 1st battalion (deployed in the Uvira operation) and Lt Col Badege as commander of its 2nd battalion (deployed to Minembwe). <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-009"></sup>

u-m23-marine-unit.name: M23 marine unit
u-m23-marine-unit.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
u-m23-marine-unit.summary: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the AFC/M23 had deployed a marine unit on Lake Tanganyika that took part in the fighting, and that after a Wazalendo attack on Monday the 'marins' of the AFC/M23 fired from the lake. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2025Q4-004"></sup> Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the AFC/M23 had deployed a marine unit on Lake Tanganyika that took part in the fighting at Makobola and its surroundings. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-SKS-FIZI-002"></sup>

u-113th-infantry-regiment.name: 113th Infantry Regiment
u-113th-infantry-regiment.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
u-113th-infantry-regiment.summary: The UN Group of Experts listed, in an annex on kamikaze drone attacks, that on 10 April at approximately 23:00 a kamikaze drone struck positions of the FARDC 113th Infantry Regiment in the Kutundu axis within Kitundu groupement (Uvira area), causing multiple FARDC casualties, and that around 23:30 a drone strike targeted FARDC positions in Muranvya, Bijombo (Uvira Territory), affecting elements of the 22nd Simba Battalion. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-044"></sup> The annex entry does not name who operated the drones; separately, its main text states that between 1 and 14 April RDF and AFC/M23 carried out at least nine drone attacks on FARDC positions in the Hauts Plateaux. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-044"></sup>

u-21e-bataillon-simba.name: 21ᵉ bataillon « Simba »
u-21e-bataillon-simba.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: SOS Médias Burundi)
u-21e-bataillon-simba.summary: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the 112 soldiers of the 21st battalion 'Simba' were prosecuted notably for abandoning, on the night of 23 August, strategic positions in the mountainous zones of Malimba and Masango in the Bijombo groupement while engaged in the defence of Uvira. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q4-007"></sup>

u-22nd-simba-battalion.name: 22nd Simba Battalion
u-22nd-simba-battalion.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The UN Group of Experts)
u-22nd-simba-battalion.summary: The UN Group of Experts listed, in an annex on kamikaze drone attacks, that on 10 April at approximately 23:00 a kamikaze drone struck positions of the FARDC 113th Infantry Regiment in the Kutundu axis within Kitundu groupement (Uvira area), causing multiple FARDC casualties, and that around 23:30 a drone strike targeted FARDC positions in Muranvya, Bijombo (Uvira Territory), affecting elements of the 22nd Simba Battalion. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-044"></sup> The annex entry does not name who operated the drones; separately, its main text states that between 1 and 14 April RDF and AFC/M23 carried out at least nine drone attacks on FARDC positions in the Hauts Plateaux. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-044"></sup>

o-acmej.name: ACMEJ
o-acmej.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Agenzia Fides)
o-acmej.summary: Agenzia Fides reported that ACMEJ's note said that from 20 October 2026 FRN soldiers and Rwandan allies stationed at Kamanyola and Katogota began attacking the villages of Katogota and Lubarika in the middle highlands, with a plan to reach Lubarika, descend to Luvungi and conquer Uvira. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q4-033"></sup>

o-acted.name: ACTED
o-acted.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)
o-acted.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that at the same press conference Corneille Nangaa said that in the night of 23 to 24 September a humanitarian convoy of UN and NGO organisations had been blocked at Mulima on its way to Minembwe, and that the convoy, headed by OCHA, ACTED and Médecins du Monde, was according to the AFC/M23 deliberately attacked by the Kinshasa coalition forces. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-M23-2026-017"></sup>

o-auditorat-militaire-superieur-du-sud-k.name: Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu
o-auditorat-militaire-superieur-du-sud-k.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi's press review)
o-auditorat-militaire-superieur-du-sud-k.summary: Radio Okapi's press review reported that the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reports the discovery of eleven mass graves in South Kivu, seven months after massacres attributed (attribués) to the M23 in the towns of Sange and Luvungi, Uvira territory; according to ACP the announcement was made on Monday 27 July by the Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu after an investigation conducted jointly with the 33rd military region. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q3-004"></sup>

o-comite-mixte-de-surveillance.name: Comité mixte de surveillance
o-comite-mixte-de-surveillance.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Mediacongo)
o-comite-mixte-de-surveillance.summary: Mediacongo reported, citing local sources, that clashes took place on Wednesday 24 June in the villages of Ilundu and Alengei between FARDC and the fighters of the Twirwaneho armed coalition and their allies; the militia accused FARDC of drone bombardments on its positions, while local actors called this a 'fuite en avant'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q2-017"></sup> It also reported that at the sixth meeting of the Joint Oversight Committee (Comité mixte de surveillance, CMS) on the security situation in the DRC, held on 24 June 2026 in London, Kinshasa and Kigali reaffirmed their commitment to defuse tensions over Minembwe. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q2-017"></sup>

o-conseil-provincial-de-securite.name: Conseil provincial de sécurité
o-conseil-provincial-de-securite.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-conseil-provincial-de-securite.summary: Radio Okapi reported that the Vice-Governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, urged all Wazalendo components to act responsibly and respect the provisions set by the Provincial Security Council, and called for the dismantling of all unauthorised barriers. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q3-016"></sup>

o-croix-rouge-de-la-rdc.name: Croix-Rouge de la RDC
o-croix-rouge-de-la-rdc.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: The ICRC)
o-croix-rouge-de-la-rdc.summary: The ICRC reported that its teams and those of the Red Cross of the DRC had received many evacuation requests for dozens of wounded people stuck notably south of Uvira city and on the highlands of Fizi territory; François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in the DRC, said its emergency surgical team that came to Fizi from Uvira had to travel six days by road when the trip could have taken three hours on the lake, and that the lack of access forced this detour. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UV-SVHC-004"></sup>

o-fec-baraka.name: FEC/Baraka
o-fec-baraka.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)
o-fec-baraka.summary: Actualite.cd reported that six civil-society actors of Baraka, including their president Etunda Maisha Albert, were released on the afternoon of 27 August from Uvira central prison; they had been arrested on 13 August at Baraka-Centre in Fizi territory and transferred to Uvira days later. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q3-017"></sup>

o-mahoro-peace.name: Mahoro Peace
o-mahoro-peace.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: SOS Médias Burundi)

timeline.text: Said in a communiqué that 32 civilians were wounded in Burundian and Congolese army offensives near Minembwe, per Kivu Morning Post

o-mahoro-peace.summary: SOS Médias Burundi published a photo captioned as showing Banyamulenge women demonstrating, placards in hand, against the blockade imposed by the Burundian army, on 4 November 2025 (place not stated in the caption); a second caption said members of the Banyamulenge community demonstrated in Indiana (USA) in December 2025, at the call of the Mahoro Peace Association, to denounce the military blockade that deprives civilians of Minembwe of food and care. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-BI-023"></sup> Kivu Morning Post reported that the humanitarian blockage at Minembwe was intensifying, with no exit and no resupply of food and medicines, and that humanitarian access was blocked. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q2-004"></sup> It said the Mahoro Peace association, which groups Congolese nationals living in the United States, had indicated that 32 civilians were wounded between 8 and 11 June. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q2-004"></sup>

g-mai-mai-mutetezi-bolingo.name: Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo
g-mai-mai-mutetezi-bolingo.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Ebuteli)
g-mai-mai-mutetezi-bolingo.summary: Ebuteli reported that on 29 January the Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara coalition and the FNL attacked the Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo in the villages of Kilumbi and Abala in Fizi territory, killing three Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-047"></sup>

o-medecins-du-monde.name: Médecins du Monde
o-medecins-du-monde.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)
o-medecins-du-monde.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that at the same press conference Corneille Nangaa said that in the night of 23 to 24 September a humanitarian convoy of UN and NGO organisations had been blocked at Mulima on its way to Minembwe, and that the convoy, headed by OCHA, ACTED and Médecins du Monde, was according to the AFC/M23 deliberately attacked by the Kinshasa coalition forces. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-ST-M23-2026-017"></sup>

o-presidence-angolaise.name: Présidence angolaise
o-presidence-angolaise.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)
o-presidence-angolaise.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Angolan Presidency announced in a communiqué on Thursday a ceasefire between Kinshasa and AFC/M23 from 18 February 2026, an announcement it said came as the FARDC had launched an offensive on several villages of Minembwe. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q1-006"></sup>

u-serpent-noir.name: Serpent noir
u-serpent-noir.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)
u-serpent-noir.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that on 17 June 2026 FARDC (supported by the Burundian army and Wazalendo) and Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23 fought on three axes around Minembwe centre: axis 1 (Mikenge to Gitavi) led by the army and Wazalendo; axis 2 (Bidegu-Kalingi) led by the special forces Hiboux and Serpent noir using combat drones; axis 3 (Kakenge) led exclusively by the Burundian army and FDLR units, according to local and security sources. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-SKS-2026Q2-002"></sup>

g-armed-defence-reserve.name: Armed Defence Reserve
g-armed-defence-reserve.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
g-armed-defence-reserve.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo announced in Uvira on Monday 7 April that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city depend exclusively from now on on the national coordinator of the Armed Defence Reserve (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q2-006"></sup>

g-imbonerakure.name: Imbonerakure
g-imbonerakure.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: SOS Médias Burundi)

timeline.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more and more young Burundians were joining Wazalendo militias in Uvira territory, with testimonies in the neighbourhoods of Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi and Kiliba, and that some refugees from the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps or the Sange transit centre had also been seen in Wazalendo ranks; it also cited regional security sources saying nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers, supported by Imbonerakure, were officially in the DRC.

g-imbonerakure.summary: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more and more young Burundians were joining Wazalendo militias in Uvira territory, with testimonies in the neighbourhoods of Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi and Kiliba, and that some refugees from the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps or the Sange transit centre had also been seen in Wazalendo ranks; it also cited regional security sources saying nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers, supported by Imbonerakure, were officially in the DRC. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q2-029"></sup>

g-mpdp.name: MPDP
g-mpdp.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Kivu Morning Post)

timeline.text: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mouvement des Patriotes pour la Défense de la Patrie (MPDP), a Wazalendo armed group, announced its creation on Saturday 11 October 2025 in the city of Uvira, South Kivu.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the MPDP is led by Pascal Biriho, alias Makanika, as commander of the forces, and by A. Byadunia Meschak Alexis as president of the political branch, and that both are former close collaborators of the warlord and former PNC officer Nyerere Bunana.

Kivu Morning Post reported that at the MPDP launch the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander while insisting on discipline and respect for the laws of the Republic, and symbolically handed a weapon to commander Pascal Biriho as a sign of support.

g-mpdp.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Mouvement des Patriotes pour la Défense de la Patrie (MPDP), a Wazalendo armed group, announced its creation on Saturday 11 October 2025 in the city of Uvira, South Kivu. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-001"></sup> Kivu Morning Post reported that at the MPDP launch the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander while insisting on discipline and respect for the laws of the Republic, and symbolically handed a weapon to commander Pascal Biriho as a sign of support. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-003"></sup>

o-ebenezer-international-ministry.name: Ebenezer International Ministry
o-ebenezer-international-ministry.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: SOS Médias Burundi)
o-ebenezer-international-ministry.summary: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Friday 21 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked the premises of the organisation Ebenezer International Ministry in Uvira, taking several electronic devices, including computers and Motorola phones. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q1-021"></sup>

o-international-contact-group-for-the-gr.name: International Contact Group for the Great Lakes
o-international-contact-group-for-the-gr.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: the cited report)
o-international-contact-group-for-the-gr.summary: The International Contact Group for the Great Lakes (United States, Belgium, Denmark, the EU, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK) urged M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and called on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2025Q4-027"></sup>

o-unhcr.name: UNHCR
o-unhcr.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Iwacu)
o-unhcr.summary: Iwacu reported that, according to UNHCR, more than 84,000 people from South Kivu had crossed into Burundi since the beginning of December 2025, bringing the total of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers in Burundi to more than 200,000, and that UNHCR declared a level 2 emergency for Burundi needing USD 33 million. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UV-CTRL-010"></sup> The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 22 May UNHCR stated that more than 1,700 'Rwandan nationals' brought to a transit center after cordon-and-search operations had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted 'under pressure'. <sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-HRC-023"></sup>

g-mai-mai-kuruninga.name: Mai-Mai Kuruninga
g-mai-mai-kuruninga.role: Armed group or force, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Ebuteli)
g-mai-mai-kuruninga.summary: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January the Mai-Mai Kuruninga killed a boy in Kalundu quarter and a man in Kabindula quarter, and the Mai-Mai Landa Bango killed a woman in Sondo quarter, in Uvira city. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-026"></sup>

u-garde-republicaine.name: Garde républicaine
u-garde-republicaine.role: Military or police unit, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Actualite.cd)

identifiers.value: 27 soldiers sentenced to death by the Uvira garrison military tribunal for cowardice before the enemy and violation of orders

u-garde-republicaine.summary: Actualite.cd reported that six women soldiers were among those convicted of violating orders and cowardice, with the sentences passed against them not specified. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q4-005"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that the public hearings of the Uvira trial opened on 15 September in flagrante procedure and concerned soldiers who fled clashes between the FARDC and fighters of the AFC/M23 coalition, RED Tabara and Twirhaneho. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q4-036"></sup>

o-international-conference-on-the-great-.name: International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR)
o-international-conference-on-the-great-.role: Organisation, as named in the cited reports (first cited: Radio Okapi)
o-international-conference-on-the-great-.summary: Radio Okapi reported, citing a MONUSCO communiqué, that MONUSCO and the ICGLR (CIRGL) were on a mission in Uvira from 23 to 27 February to prepare deployment of the joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism, and quoted acting Special Representative Vivian Van de Perre as saying MONUSCO's mandate in South Kivu is focused on ceasefire monitoring and does not include protection of civilians. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UV-2026Q1-019"></sup> Al Jazeera, citing AFP and Reuters, reported that on Monday the UN and government sources said a ceasefire monitoring team had arrived to track the Qatari-mediated truce, and that the UN said the mission had deployed to Minembwe in South Kivu, where intense fighting had persisted in recent months. <sup class="cm" data-c="r1-POL-2026-016"></sup>

p-lawrence-kanyuka.name: Lawrence Kanyuka
p-lawrence-kanyuka.role: AFC/M23 spokesperson and head of communication (later described as FRN spokesperson), per Actualite.cd, the UN Group of Experts and Chimp Reports

identifiers.value: M23 civilian spokesperson and public relations officer for the Congo River Alliance
head of the communication department and spokesperson of the AFC/M23 rebellion

timeline.text: Sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury (OFAC), which described him as M23 civilian spokesperson
The UN Group of Experts reported that Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed a France24 report on the Katindo killings as fake news and denied having spoken to France24.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 head of communication and spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement questioned the credibility, impartiality and objectivity of the latest Human Rights Watch report on Uvira.
Actualite.cd reported that Lawrence Kanyuka announced on 17 May that AFC-M23 confirmed a case of Ebola virus disease in Goma.
Said the 7 June 2026 bombings by the 'coalition FARDC-FDNB' on Ilundu/Basita killed several civilians
Bwiza reported that Lawrence Kanyuka said FDLR fighters attacked civilians at Mulala in Rutshuru territory on the night of 31 August.
As FRN spokesperson, said Kinshasa coalition forces were bombarding Rugezi, per Kivu Morning Post
Chimp Reports reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka confirmed on 27 October that Kamanzi had joined the FRN military wing.
Confirmed that Kamanzi had joined the FRN's military wing, per Chimp Reports

p-lawrence-kanyuka.summary: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 head of communication and spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement questioned the credibility, impartiality and objectivity of the latest Human Rights Watch report on Uvira.<sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-UV-SVHC-010"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed a France24 report on the Katindo killings as fake news and denied having spoken to France24.<sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-021"></sup> Actualite.cd reported that Lawrence Kanyuka announced on 17 May that AFC-M23 confirmed a case of Ebola virus disease in Goma.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-POL-2026-009"></sup>

p-bertrand-bisimwa.name: Bertrand Bisimwa
p-bertrand-bisimwa.role: AFC/M23 president and AFC deputy coordinator (later FRN vice-president), per Actualite.cd, Kivu Morning Post and the UN Group of Experts

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa admitted the existence of regular daily and nocturnal patrols sweeping Goma but claimed they were carried out lawfully, in a statement published on X on 9 March 2025.

The EU listed Bertrand Bisimwa on 17 March 2025 (Implementing Regulation 2025/509), describing him as leader (president) of the political branch of the M23, born 8 September 1972 in Bukavu, Congolese, and stating that he holds a leading position as President of the M23.
Kivu Morning Post reported that decisions reorganising the South Kivu administration were signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, president of the M23 and deputy coordinator of the AFC.
Actualite.cd reported that AFC deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa, at a press conference in Goma on 7 August 2025, called a UN report on an alleged massacre in Rutshuru non factuel.
BBC Afrique reported that Bertrand Bisimwa said the withdrawal from Uvira was underway.
Kivu Morning Post reported that the FRN vice-presidents Corneille Nangaa and Bertrand Bisimwa presented the FRN organisation in Goma on 21 October.

p-bertrand-bisimwa.summary: Actualite.cd reported that AFC deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa, at a press conference in Goma on 7 August 2025, called a UN report on an alleged massacre in Rutshuru non factuel.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-004"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa admitted the existence of regular daily and nocturnal patrols sweeping Goma but claimed they were carried out lawfully, in a statement published on X on 9 March 2025.<sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-446-022"></sup> Kivu Morning Post reported that decisions reorganising the South Kivu administration were signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, president of the M23 and deputy coordinator of the AFC.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-004"></sup>

p-corneille-nangaa.name: Corneille Nangaa
p-corneille-nangaa.role: AFC/M23 political coordinator (later FRN vice-president), per BBC, Kivu Morning Post and the UN Group of Experts

identifiers.value: coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo
leader of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC)
UN Security Council sanctions listing (1533 Committee)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that the graduation ceremony at Rumangabo was presided over by Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa.
The UN Group of Experts reported that on 23 October AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa publicly denied allegations made by Twangiza Mining SA.
The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 December 2025 AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted a statement on X announcing that AFC/M23 would unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira.

Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in Goma on 20 February that the authorities in Goma were the first to ask for the reopening of the Goma international airport.
Listed in the SECO consolidated annex as the leader of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC)
Top Africa News reported that African Union facilitators met political coordinator Corneille Nangaa and his deputies in Goma.

p-corneille-nangaa.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 December 2025 AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted a statement on X announcing that AFC/M23 would unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira.<sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-466-012"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that on 23 October AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa publicly denied allegations made by Twangiza Mining SA.<sup class="cm" data-c="r2-G-DOC-858-026"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that the graduation ceremony at Rumangabo was presided over by Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UC-M23-018"></sup>

p-sultani-makenga.name: Sultani Makenga
p-sultani-makenga.role: AFC/M23 military chief and coordinator, per the UN Group of Experts, Human Rights Watch and Radio Okapi

identifiers.value: Military leader of the Mouvement du 23 Mars (M23) group
UK asset freeze (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime)

timeline.text: The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Sultani Makenga (a.k.a. 'MAKENGA, Colonel, Sultani') with the position 'Military leader of the Mouvement du 23 Mars (M23) group operating in the Democratic Republic of the Congo'.
Radio Okapi reported that M23 rebels under the command of Makenga launched an operation to hunt alleged FDLR rebels at Kahumiro.
The Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 General Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 elite police force named Police révolutionnaire congolaise.
The Group of Experts reported that the offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr Makenga and Mr Byamungu.
Kivu Morning Post reported that the military coordinator of the AFC/M23 and ARC chief of staff, General-Major Sultani Makenga, told senior cadres in Goma on 29 December to be in a state of war.
BBC Gahuza, relaying Reuters, reported that Gen Sultani Makenga escaped unharmed from the drone strike that killed Willy Ngoma near Rubaya.

p-sultani-makenga.summary: Kivu Morning Post reported that the military coordinator of the AFC/M23 and ARC chief of staff, General-Major Sultani Makenga, told senior cadres in Goma on 29 December to be in a state of war.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-019"></sup> The Group of Experts reported that the offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr Makenga and Mr Byamungu.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-GOE-004"></sup> Radio Okapi reported that M23 rebels under the command of Makenga launched an operation to hunt alleged FDLR rebels at Kahumiro.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-012"></sup>

p-baudoin-ngaruye.name: Baudoin Ngaruye
p-baudoin-ngaruye.role: AFC/M23 commander of the First Defence Zone, per the UN Group of Experts; described by Human Rights Watch as under UN sanctions

identifiers.value: commander of the AFC/M23 First Defence Zone
Military Leader of the movement du Mars (M23)
UK sanctions (UK Sanctions List ref DRC0024)

timeline.text: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 military operations in Binza were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Colonel Samuel Mushagara and Brigadier General Baudoin Ngaruye respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions.

The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Baudoin Ngaruye Wa Myamuro with the title 'Military Leader of the movement du Mars (M23)' and the position 'Brigadier General' (UN ref CDi.019).

The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September Brigadier General Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of the AFC/M23 First Defense Zone covering the Goma-Rutshuru-Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities.
The UN Group of Experts reported that the AFC/M23 First Defence Zone command was led by Brigadier General Baudoin Ngaruye.
The Group of Experts reported that a first AFC/M23 defence zone covering Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories was led by General Baudoin Ngaruye.

p-baudoin-ngaruye.summary: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September Brigadier General Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of the AFC/M23 First Defense Zone covering the Goma-Rutshuru-Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-004"></sup> The UN Group of Experts reported that the AFC/M23 First Defence Zone command was led by Brigadier General Baudoin Ngaruye.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-003"></sup> Human Rights Watch reported that M23 military operations in Binza were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Colonel Samuel Mushagara and Brigadier General Baudoin Ngaruye respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions.<sup class="cm" data-c="r1-NKS-2025Q3-002"></sup>

p-bernard-byamungu.name: Bernard Byamungu
p-bernard-byamungu.role: AFC/M23 general described as the movement number two and as commander for South Kivu, per Actualite.cd and the UN Group of Experts; identity across spellings follows the cited claims

identifiers.value: leader of the AFC/M23 third defence zone (South Kivu)
Deputy Commander of operations and intelligence for M23

timeline.text: The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Bernard Maheshe Byamungu (a.k.a. TIGER ONE) with the positions 'Brigadier General' and 'Deputy Commander of operations and intelligence for M23', and its narrative says he was promoted in January 2023 to Brigadier for the Congolese Revolutionary Army and then appointed chief of staff and deputy to Sultani Makenga.
Actualite.cd reported that General Bernard Byamungu, described as the movement number two, held a public meeting at Nzibira in Walungu territory.
The Group of Experts reported that the offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr Makenga and Mr Byamungu.
Kivu Morning Post reported that more than 100 Mai-Mai fighters surrendered to AFC/M23 in Uvira in the presence of General Byamungu Maheshe, described as deputy commander of the AFC/M23.
FNTV reported that it could give a clear denial that General Bernard Byamungu of the AFC/M23 had died.
Enquete.cd reported, according to sources close to the rebellion, that Bernard Maheshe Byamungu, alias Tiger One, had died, a report that FNTV denied on 23 May.

p-willy-ngoma.name: Willy Ngoma
p-willy-ngoma.role: AFC/M23 military spokesperson, per the UN Group of Experts and BBC Afrique; reported killed in a drone strike near Rubaya

identifiers.value: UK asset freeze (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime)

timeline.text: The UN Group of Experts reported that military spokesperson Willy Ngoma was present when AFC/M23 publicly burned identification documents of refugees.

The UK consolidated list of financial sanctions targets (Democratic Republic of the Congo regime, last updated 15 August 2025) lists Willy Ngoma with the positions 'Major' and 'Military spokesperson for M23'.

p-makanaki-kasimbira-john.name: Makanaki Kasimbira John
p-makanaki-kasimbira-john.role: Wazalendo figure called General Makanaki in Uvira, per SOS Médias Burundi and the UN Group of Experts

timeline.text: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Wazalendo-affiliated fighters under the command of generals Mayele and Makanaki had multiplied acts of pillage in quarters of Uvira.
SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a 17-minute audio message broadcast on 19 July, General Makanaki, described as an influential Wazalendo figure, said any truck coming from Bukavu must be stopped.

Kivu Morning Post reported that general 'Muzalendo' Makanaki Kasimbira, in a viral video, denounced General Gasita, saying: 'Here in Uvira, we refuse this disorder of sending us foreign faces, people who do not look like Congolese. If they have their Rwandan commanders, we will not accept them here in Uvira.'

RFI said that the Wazalendo groups at Uvira are led by known and feared militia chiefs, citing among them the former FARDC member René Itongwa, the former soldier and CNPSC leader William Amuri Yakutumba, sanctioned by the UN, and John Makanaki Kasimbira, whom it described as long installed in the hills overlooking Uvira and very hostile to General Olivier Gasita, deputy commander of the 33rd military region.

Tumaini Africa News reported that the 'self-proclaimed lieutenant general' Makanaki said, in the same press briefing at Uvira, that the incentive payment was a pleasant surprise and a real comfort for the Wazalendo.
The UN Group of Experts reported on old warlords actively engaged on the frontlines, including William Yakutumba, Makanaki Kasimbira John, Delphin Ngomanzito, René Itongwa and Ilunga.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Dunia Mwamba, congratulated the MPDP commander at its launch.

Kivu Morning Post reported that the RAD provincial coordinator, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, announced on Thursday 22 January 2026 security measures for Uvira: at a press conference he formally banned carrying firearms and bladed weapons in urban areas and the erection of illegal roadblocks by self-defence groups, demanded the immediate withdrawal of the Wazalendo from the city centre, and said that urban security now fell exclusively under the PNC and the Military Police; the outlet added that the RAD was setting up a special unit to secure the city.

Tumaini Africa News reported that the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, accompanied by representatives of the VDP Wazalendo, expressed gratitude to President Tshisekedi and the central government for a 325 US dollar incentive payment called 'effort de guerre', in a press briefing held in Kalundu commune, Uvira city.

The Agence Congolaise de Presse (ACP), the state news agency, reported from a Ministry of the Interior workshop at Uvira that Willian Amuri Yakutumba, whom ACP described as coordinator of the 'Wazalendo' in South Kivu province, said that not all armed persons are Wazalendo and that the Wazalendo must be distinguished from other armed groups or individuals in South Kivu; ACP also described Alexis Dunia as 'also coordinator of wazalendo'.

o-conseil-local-jeunesse-itombwe.summary: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing figures from the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe after monitoring, that at least 23 people were killed, 17 seriously wounded and at least six villages burned from 10 to 27 August 2026 in fighting in the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory.<sup class="cm" data-c="r6-F-FIZ-003"></sup> Radio Maendeleo also reported that the council counted at least 1100 households, more than six thousand people, displaced in the bush or in host villages.<sup class="cm" data-c="r6-F-FIZ-004"></sup>
